items.defectStatement: In `.group-member-info .name` (line 522) the light-theme argument was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`, so in light themes the member name now renders as a medium-primary tint instead of the intended darker primary, reducing contrast. The finding is correct; the sibling `.title` rule (line 527) legitimately uses 50% and is not part of this defect.
obligations: The light-theme argument of the `dark-light-choose(...)` on line 522 must be `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, restoring the 30% lightness.

The dark-theme support added on line 522 must be preserved (still wrapped in `dark-light-choose`), with a light tint of the dark-theme background color, e.g. `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)`.
The rule may only change its `color` declaration; `display: inline-block` and `margin-top: 5px` on lines 520-521 must remain unchanged.
No other selector's color must be changed (in particular `.title` at line 527 and the `.notification .fa/.icon` rule at line 514 keep their existing 50% values).
items.notes: The cited code matches the finding. Only line 522 is in scope; the other `dark-light-choose` additions in the diff (lines 462, 514, 527, etc.) are intentional dark-theme support and should not be reverted to plain `scale-color`. A fix that keeps `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` is the canonical answer; graders should accept equivalent dark-theme tints as long as the light-theme 30% value is restored.

items.defectStatement: BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up blocked addresses with an exact, case-sensitive `where(email: email)` comparison, so a blocked entry stored as `bad@spammers.org` is not matched when the submitted address is `Bad@Spammers.org`, allowing a block to be bypassed by changing case.
obligations: BlockedEmail.should_block?(email) must return the block action for a stored blocked address regardless of the case of the supplied email (e.g. 'Bad@Spammers.org' must match a stored 'bad@spammers.org').
The existing side effects of a match must be preserved: match_count is incremented, last_match_at is set to the current time, and the record is saved.
The return semantics must be unchanged: a matched record with action_type == block returns truthy; a matched record with action_type do_nothing, or no match, returns falsy.
The call must not raise on nil or blank input (compare safely rather than calling downcase on nil directly).
items.notes: The finding is accurate about the case-sensitivity of the comparison at line 12. The claim about User.new_from_params not downcasing is outside the shown window and is not verifiable here, but the query itself is still case-sensitive regardless. Multiple fixes are valid: normalizing in the query (e.g. lower(email) = ? with email.to_s.downcase) or normalizing the attribute/callers; a query-side normalization is the minimal fix and does not require a data migration. Note that a stored-side-only fix requires both normalizing on write and a backfill, and would not help if callers still pass mixed case. The case-sensitive `validates :email, uniqueness: true` at line 5 has a similar weakness but is not part of the cited line and need not be changed.

items.defectStatement: In `perform_retrieve` (lib/topic_retriever.rb:40-42), an embed request synchronously runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`, which loops over every `rss.items` entry and runs the full `TopicEmbed.import` path (DB lookups plus topic/post creation) for each one, with no early exit once the requested `@embed_url` has been imported. So a feed of N items costs O(N) heavy writes to satisfy one embed view, even when the wanted item is the first item.
obligations: Polling must stop doing import work as soon as the requested `@embed_url` has been imported (or must only process the item(s) matching `@embed_url`), instead of importing the entire feed.

The post-poll behavior of `perform_retrieve` must be preserved: after the feed poll, if `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` return true, otherwise fall through to `fetch_http`; the pre-poll exists? bail-out at line 37 and the `feed_polling_enabled?` gate remain unchanged in effect.

Other callers of `Jobs::PollFeed` (e.g. the scheduled feed poll that previously called `execute({})` with no target URL) must keep working and still poll the whole feed when no specific embed_url is given.
An unknown/absent embed_url must not silently skip the fallback HTTP fetch: if the feed poll does not produce the requested embed, `fetch_http` still runs.
items.notes: The cited lines alone are not sufficient to fix this; a valid fix will typically also touch the poll_feed job (e.g. accept an `embed_url:` argument and/or break out of the items loop on match) while keeping backward compatibility with the empty-args call. The finding is accurate; note it concerns the synchronous execution inside `perform_retrieve`, not the trailing `exists?` check, which only observes the damage after the whole feed has already been processed.

items.defectStatement: In `totalPages` (app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6, lines 11-14), `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` adds a page even when `user_count` divides evenly by `limit` (e.g. 50 members with limit 25 yields 3 instead of 2). Because `showingLast` compares `currentPage` to this inflated value, the real last page is not recognized as last, and `next` can advance `offset` to `user_count`, landing on an empty page.
obligations: `totalPages` must return 0 when `user_count` is 0 (empty-group case preserved).
For a `user_count` that is an exact multiple of `limit`, `totalPages` must equal `user_count / limit` (no extra page): e.g. 50/25 -> 2, 25/25 -> 1.
For a `user_count` that is not an exact multiple of `limit`, `totalPages` must still round up (one page beyond the floor): e.g. 30/25 -> 2, 1/25 -> 1.

The computed property must continue to depend on both `limit` and `user_count` so it recomputes when either changes; `currentPage` and the `showingLast`/`showingFirst` bindings must keep working against the corrected value.
items.notes: `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` is the minimal correct fix and satisfies all obligations; any equivalent expression (e.g. `Math.floor((user_count + limit - 1) / limit)`) is equally valid. The second half of the finding (guarding `next` with `offset + limit >= user_count`) is outside the cited lines and is not required once `totalPages` is corrected: with the correct count, `showingLast` is true on the real last page so `next` returns early. A defensive guard there is acceptable but should not replace the `totalPages` fix. Verify the `user_count == 0` short-circuit is retained (ceil form alone would return 0 for 0 anyway, but the explicit guard is existing behavior).

items.defectStatement: In `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` (app/models/embedable_host.rb:10-18), the lookup key is `uri.host`, which drops any port, while `validates_format_of :host` (line 2) and `before_validation` (lines 5-8) both allow a stored host to contain an explicit `:port`. A record saved as `example.com:8080` therefore never matches the incoming referer/embed URL `http://example.com:8080/...`, so `record_for_host` returns nil and `host_allowed?` silently denies embedding for that entry.
obligations: When the incoming URL carries an explicit port (e.g. `http://example.com:8080/page`), `record_for_host` must match a stored record whose host is `example.com:8080` (same port), in addition to any no-port behavior.

Existing behavior for hosts without ports must be preserved: a stored `example.com` must still match `http://example.com/path`, `https://example.com`, and other URLs whose port is the scheme default or absent.

`record_for_host` must keep returning the matched record (or nil/false when nothing matches) and must not raise on nil, blank, malformed, or non-URI input (`URI(...) rescue nil` path must still yield `false`).

The lookup must remain a single query against the `host` column using the same case-insensitive comparison style already present (`lower(host) = ...`), i.e. the fix must not require schema or caller changes in `host_allowed?`.
items.notes: Trap: `URI('http://example.com/x').port` returns 80 even when no port is written, so a naive `host + ':' + uri.port` breaks every no-port record; the port may only be appended when the URL text explicitly contains one (or when it differs from the scheme default). The finding is accurate as written; the only nuance is that it applies to both referer and embed URL callers via `host_allowed?`. A valid alternative fix is to strip/reject ports at validation time, but since this finding cites lines 10-18, the expected change is in `record_for_host`. Unrelated pre-existing quirk (not part of this finding): the query uses `lower(host) = ?` without downcasing the bound value, so mixed-case input is not actually matched case-insensitively.

items.defectStatement: In Discourse.Utilities.validateUploadedFile (utilities.js lines 180-186), the upload size limit was replaced with a hardcoded 10 * 1024 KB constant, discarding the per-type lookup Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']. As a result the client no longer honors max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb: uploads larger than the configured limit for either type are accepted up to 10 MB, and images are rejected above 10 MB even when the configured limit is higher.
obligations: maxSizeKB must be derived from the configured site setting for the given type, e.g. Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], rather than a literal 10 * 1024; both the 'image' and 'attachment' cases of the type argument must be honored.

The size check must remain fileSizeKB = file.size / 1024 and the comparison fileSizeKB > maxSizeKB; the units of maxSizeKB must stay in KB so the bootbox message I18n.t('post.errors.file_too_large', { max_size_kb: maxSizeKB }) reports the correct configured value.
Failure behavior must be preserved: on exceeding the limit, alert via bootbox with the configured max_size_kb and return false; on passing, fall through to the final 'return true'.
The preceding authorized-extension check and the bypassNewUserRestriction / isAllowedToUploadAFile(newuser) logic must remain unchanged.
items.notes: The file diff shows an identical hardcoding was also introduced in displayErrorForUpload's 413 handler (currently around line 246, outside the cited lines); it is the same class of defect but is not required to be fixed to satisfy these obligations, since the grader replaces only the cited lines 180-186. Any fix that reads the setting under a local alias (e.g. var max = Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'];) is equally valid as a direct lookup. Beware that SiteSettings values may be numeric strings; the existing numeric comparison relies on JS coercion, so do not 'fix' that with extra parsing that could break the comparison.

items.defectStatement: Line 17 makes the I18n fallback chain depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so translations can resolve to whatever the site locale is at request time; but the downstream translate_accelerator LRU cache key does not include default_locale, so after an admin changes the default locale, users whose strings were falling back to the old site locale continue to receive the previously cached text.
obligations: The fallback order produced by FallbackLocaleList#[] must remain [requested locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en], de-duplicated and nil-free (uniq/compact semantics preserved).

After SiteSetting.default_locale changes, subsequent translations must resolve against the new default locale rather than returning stale cached fallback text (e.g. by incorporating default_locale into the cache key or clearing the I18n cache when the setting changes).

FallbackLocaleList#[] must remain a callable Hash-subclass method returning an ordered Array of locales, and ensure_loaded! must continue to iterate the fallback list for the current I18n.locale without raising.
No change to the behavior for users whose locale already has the requested translation, and no change to the :en terminal fallback.
items.notes: The cited line 17 is the fallback-order definition, not the translate_accelerator cache key itself; the finding's mechanism is plausible but its stated fix may legitimately land in a different file/initializer. A grader should accept either of the two suggested approaches (key-busting default_locale or cache invalidation on setting change) provided obligation 2 holds, and should not require line 17 itself to be the only edit site. Overstatement to watch: the finding asserts 'now depends on' as if newly introduced, but the dependency on SiteSetting.default_locale is intended behavior; the actual defect is only the caching/invalidation gap.

items.defectStatement: The `unsubscribe` action mutates persistent state (it loads a TopicUser and calls `tu.save!` to lower the user's notification level) while being routable as a plain GET; because the action was added to `skip_before_filter :check_xhr` and GET requests are not covered by Rails' CSRF check, a third-party page can point a link or image at /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and carry out the change using only the logged-in user's cookies.
obligations: The state-changing request must not be executable cross-site from an ambient-cookie GET: either require a non-GET (POST/PUT) request whose authenticity is verified by a CSRF token, or require a per-user signed token in the request that a third party cannot forge. Leaving the action reachable as an unprotected GET, or relying only on Rails' default forgery protection (which does not apply to GET), does not satisfy this.
The intended notification-level transition must be preserved: if the existing TopicUser.notification_level is above `regular`, set it to `regular`; otherwise set it to `muted`.

Existing non-mutating behavior must be preserved: when the slug does not match or is blank for a non-JSON request, the action still redirects to the topic's unsubscribe URL with status 301, and on success it still calls `perform_show_response` (JSON responses for `format.json` included).

The action must remain reachable in the normal in-app flow it was added for (the client/UI that triggers it, and the `check_xhr` skip it relies on) without requiring the user to be re-authenticated or to visit an interstitial in a way that breaks that flow.
items.notes: Valid fixes include: changing the route/action to POST/PUT and letting CSRF protection apply (adding `unsubscribe` back to the XHR/CSRF-checked set instead of skipping it), or keeping the GET but requiring a signed per-user token (e.g. a verifier-based URL) verified in the action. The finding's core claim is accurate; note that Rails' `protect_from_forgery` never applies to GET, so a fix that only adds a CSRF token without changing the HTTP method does not fix it. Modern SameSite=Lax cookies block pure cross-site subresource fetches but still send cookies on top-level link navigations, so they mitigate but do not close this hole. Separately, the cited code has no nil-guard on `tu` (a user with no TopicUser row gets a NoMethodError 500) and assumes `current_user` is present; a correct security fix need not address these, but a fix that does handle them is not wrong.

items.defectStatement: In the final else branch (lines 147-150), the same-domain test is one-directional: discourse_host.ends_with?('.' << website_host) is true only when the instance hostname is a subdomain of the website host (e.g. website example.com, instance forum.example.com). When the website host is instead a subdomain of the instance host (e.g. website forum.example.com, instance example.com), the test is false, so the method falls back to the bare website_host and drops the distinguishing URI path, behaving differently from the exact-match and equal-label sibling branches above.
obligations: When the website host is a subdomain of the instance hostname, e.g. website 'forum.example.com' with instance 'example.com' (or 'www.example.com' with 'example.com', the case where the instance has fewer labels), website_name must return website_host + URI(website.to_s).path, not the bare host.

Preserve the existing matching cases: identical hosts and equal-label sibling hosts (e.g. www.example.com vs forum.example.com) must still return host plus path; hosts that are not in the same domain must still return the bare host.

Do not introduce suffix false positives: a website host that merely ends with the instance hostname string without a dot boundary (e.g. website 'notexample.com' or 'ample.com' with instance 'example.com') must not be treated as a subdomain and must not gain the path.
Keep the method's existing interface and guard behavior: return nil when website_host cannot be parsed, and leave include_website_name unchanged.
items.notes: The finding is accurate about the cited lines. A minimal valid fix is to broaden the else condition to also match website_host.ends_with?('.' + discourse_host) (the dot boundary is essential; a bare ends_with?(discourse_host) would wrongly match 'notexample.com'). Alternatively, restructure to compare the shared domain suffix in both directions. Note the equal-label-count branch already handles symmetric sibling hosts, so the reverse check is only needed for differing label counts. A grader should accept any implementation that satisfies the obligations for the forum.example.com/example.com case without breaking the unrelated-host cases.

items.defectStatement: In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb lines 144-146, `website_name` treats two hosts as same-domain whenever their full label count is equal (>2) and the labels after the first are identical. On multi-label public suffixes such as `co.uk`, `forum.co.uk` and `evil.co.uk` both reduce to `co.uk`, so an unrelated website is treated as same-domain and `URI(website.to_s).path` is appended; the method should return only `website_host` for such unrelated hosts.
obligations: For unrelated registrable domains under a multi-label public suffix (e.g. `forum.co.uk` vs `evil.co.uk`, or `foo.com.au` vs `bar.com.au`), `website_name` must return only `website_host` and must not append the URI path.

For hosts that do share the same registrable domain across subdomains (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`, and likewise `www.example.co.uk` vs `forum.example.co.uk`), `website_name` must still append the URI path.

Existing exact-host and parent-domain behavior must be preserved: `website_host == discourse_host` and `discourse_host.ends_with?("." + website_host)` should still append the path; all other host combinations should return only `website_host`; a nil website host should still return nil.
The serializer inclusion behavior (`include_website_name` / `website.present?`) must remain unchanged.
items.notes: Valid fixes may use the public_suffix gem / a public suffix list, or any equivalent registrable-domain comparison. The finding's suggestion of 'requiring at least three labels after removing the subdomain' is imprecise and can break the common `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` case, so grade by behavior rather than a specific algorithm. The code appends host+path rather than the scheme, but the observable issue is that an unrelated host's path is exposed.

items.defectStatement: In EmbedController#best (lines 14-16), when no TopicEmbed exists for the supplied embed_url, the controller unconditionally enqueues :retrieve_topic for every request; the cited code contains no rate limit, per-URL in-progress/dedupe guard, or other bound. Because the endpoint only validates the referer host and permits anonymous users, unauthenticated traffic can create unbounded retrieve_topic jobs and associated feed/HTTP fetches by requesting many distinct embed_url values or repeatedly hitting a not-yet-imported URL.
obligations: Repeated requests for the same unseen embed_url must not enqueue more than one retrieval job within a bounded window while a retrieval is pending/in progress.
Distinct unseen embed_urls from unauthenticated traffic must be bounded by rate limiting, global/IP throttling, or equivalent deduplication so a client cannot cause unbounded job fanout.
If retrieval triggers a feed poll or remote HTTP fetch, that work must be performed at most once per interval per source/feed, not once per retrieval request.

Preserve existing valid behavior: known topic_id still builds TopicView with best:5; the first valid unseen embed_url still enqueues retrieval and renders loading; ensure_embeddable/layout/discourse_expires_in behavior remains intact.
items.notes: The shown lines have no throttle at all, so the finding's 'throttle keyed only on exact URL' is not visible here; the concrete defect is unconditional enqueueing. A valid fix may live in the controller or in job/scheduler-level deduplication/rate limiting; grade for bounded enqueue/fetch behavior, not a specific implementation. TopicRetriever/PollFeed internals are outside the shown code; the impact depends on that external behavior, but the controller-level unbounded enqueue remains. ensure_embeddable validates referer host, not authentication, so anonymous traffic is in scope.

items.defectStatement: In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss line 102 (inside the .custom-message-length rule), the dark-light-choose arguments are inverted: the light-theme branch was changed to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and the dark-theme branch to scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%). The original declaration was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) and the matching desktop/modal.scss rule uses (70%, 30%), so the mobile light and dark values are both wrong/mismatched with desktop.
obligations: The light-theme (first) argument of dark-light-choose must keep the original light-theme appearance, i.e. scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), not 30%.
The dark-theme (second) argument must use $secondary with lightness 30% (i.e. scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)), matching the desktop/modal.scss rule's (70%, 30%) pairing.
The declaration must remain the `color` property of the .custom-message-length selector; the margin and font-size declarations in that rule must be unchanged.
dark-light-choose must remain the wrapper (light/dark theming behavior preserved), not a bare scale-color as it was originally.
items.notes: Cited-code-only: the shown line is exactly the buggy line; a correct fix is dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). Several equivalent orderings/expressions are acceptable as long as the light branch resolves to the original 70% $primary and the dark branch to $secondary 30%. The finding's claim that the desktop rule is the reference matches the described (70%, 30%) convention; grader should confirm light = first arg = 70% and dark = second arg = 30%.

items.defectStatement: The client-side `topic-unsubscribe` route's `model` hook only calls `PostStream.loadTopicView`, which fetches ordinary topic JSON; nothing in the route performs the notification-level change. A client-side transition to this route therefore renders the unsubscribe confirmation page without actually unsubscribing the user, whereas the equivalent server-rendered/full page request does change the preference. The finding is accurate as to the shown code (the hook contains no preference-changing call and there is no other action in the file doing so).
obligations: A transition into this route must issue a request that actually changes the topic's notification level to the unsubscribed state for the topic identified by `params.id`; the topic-view fetch alone does not satisfy this.

The hook must still resolve to a topic model populated via `topic.updateFromJson(json)` from the topic-view payload, so the existing template and downstream `afterModel`/`didTransition` behavior (`details.notificationReasonText`, `showFooter`) keep working.
If the preference-changing request fails, the route must not present the unsubscribe as completed (no false success); the error should surface or be handled before the confirmation state is shown.
The change must be scoped to the single topic in `params.id` and must not alter notification levels of any other topic; it should be safe/idempotent with respect to the user's current level.
items.notes: Valid alternatives exist: the route could call the topic model's unsubscribe/notification-level API before returning the topic, or it could deliberately avoid auto-unsubscribing and instead require an explicit user submission on this page (in which case the rendered page must clearly require the action and no success is implied by the transition itself). If graded strictly against the cited lines 4-8, the model hook is the expected place for the request. Do not treat the existing `createRecord` + `loadTopicView` + `updateFromJson` + return-topic structure as a defect; it must be preserved. The finding's factual claim that a client-side transition leaves the level unchanged is consistent with the shown code; its parenthetical 'or require an explicit submission' is an acceptable alternative fix, not an additional bug.

items.defectStatement: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, the anchor branch at lines 64-66 rewrites any href beginning with '/' using `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"`, so protocol-relative hrefs such as `//cdn.example.com/a.png` become `http://embedhost/cdn.example.com/a.png`, pointing at the embed host instead of the external CDN and breaking external links. The identical defect exists for img src at lines 70-72, which the finding correctly notes.
obligations: Protocol-relative URLs (`//host/path`, for both `a[href]` and `img[src]`) must not be rewritten to `#{prefix}/host/path`; they must either be left unchanged or resolved as scheme-relative against the source scheme (e.g. `http://cdn.example.com/a.png`).

Genuinely root-relative URLs (single leading slash, e.g. `/images/a.png`) must still be rewritten to `#{prefix}/images/a.png`, preserving existing behavior including the stripping of extra leading slashes.
Absolute and non-relative values must remain untouched: `http://...`, `https://...`, `mailto:`, fragment-only `#...`, and empty/absent attributes must not be modified.
The same protocol-relative handling must be applied to `img[src]` (lines 70-72) as to `a[href]`, so both element types behave consistently.
items.notes: The cited code and the finding agree, so the finding is accurate and not overstated. Two fixes are equally valid and a grader should accept either: (a) skip the rewrite when the value starts with '//' (leaving the browser to resolve it), or (b) special-case `//` into a proper absolute URL using the source URI scheme (e.g. `"#{uri.scheme}:#{href}"`). The obligation only requires that `//host/path` never collapse into `#{prefix}/host/path`. Also verify the fix does not accidentally treat a single '/' as protocol-relative (e.g. avoid a regex like `/^\/+/` that matches both); a `start_with?('//')` check or equivalent is needed, and the img branch must be changed in the same commit.

items.defectStatement: At line 497 the `.group-member-info .name` color rule was changed to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, but the light-theme value on the first branch was previously `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`; using 50% lightness makes the name text noticeably lighter than before and silently regresses the light theme. (The dark-theme wrapping itself is fine; the regression is the changed light-branch lightness.)
obligations: The light-theme (first) argument of the `dark-light-choose(...)` on the cited `color` declaration must be `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` — the previously existing 30% value, not 50%.
The declaration must still provide a distinct dark-theme value via the second `dark-light-choose` argument, derived from `$secondary` (so dark mode does not fall back to a `$primary`-based color).

The selector/target must remain the `color` of `.group-member-info .name` inside this file; no other declarations (e.g. `.title` at line 503 or `.fa, .icon` at line 489, whose original light values were 50%) should be altered.
The fix must remain valid SCSS that compiles in this asset pipeline (dark-light-choose with two color arguments).
items.notes: The finding's suggested dark value `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` is one valid choice, but the grader should accept any `$secondary`-derived dark-theme value, since the pre-change rule had no dark variant and the only hard regression is the light branch dropping from 30% to 50%. Do not flag the new dark-light-choose wrapping itself as a bug.

items.defectStatement: In the save success callback (lines 37-38), host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))) derives the displayed category from the submitted categoryId rather than from the server response. When a new host is saved with no category selected, categoryId is null (the default), so findById(null) yields no category and the client clears the category the server just assigned (uncategorized), leaving the row empty until reload.
obligations: After a successful save, host.category must reflect the category actually assigned by the server, including the uncategorized case when no category was selected; it must not become null/undefined solely because the submitted categoryId was null.
When a category is selected, the displayed category must still be the selected one (existing behavior preserved).
The fix must apply to both new hosts (categoryId defaults to null) and edits of existing hosts.
The success path must still clear editToggled (set it to false) and leave the .catch(popupAjaxError) error handling intact.
items.notes: Valid fixes include using the payload returned by host.save, reading the server-assigned category_id off the saved host, or only calling findById when categoryId is non-null (falling back to the response/saved record). Note the submitted value is legitimately null for uncategorized, so guards that skip the set when categoryId is null are acceptable only if the record already carries the correct category from the response. The finding correctly describes the callback; no overstatement to correct.

items.defectStatement: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (no-arg, lines 64-71) delegates to hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). Because hasPermission returns true when ANY of the supplied scopes is granted, a subject holding only the all-groups VIEW permission is reported as able to manage all groups, so manage endpoints that gate on canManage()/requireManage() grant read-only group viewers create/update/delete privileges. The sibling canManage(GroupModel) uses MANAGE alone, confirming the VIEW scope here is unintended.
obligations: canManage() (no-arg) must authorize only on the all-groups MANAGE permission (AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) and must return false when the subject has only VIEW for all groups.
The existing root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS) short-circuit returning true must be preserved.
canView() and canView(GroupModel) must continue to accept either VIEW or MANAGE (that dual-scope behavior is legitimate and must not be changed).
The group-specific canManage(GroupModel) behavior (MANAGE only, plus MANAGE_USERS role short-circuit) must remain unchanged.
items.notes: Finding is accurate; cited lines match the file window. The minimal correct fix is to drop AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW from the call to hasPermission in canManage(). Alternative forms are acceptable (e.g., a direct policy/permission evaluation for MANAGE) as long as MANAGE-only semantics and the MANAGE_USERS role bypass are kept. Do not 'fix' by editing canView/canView(GroupModel) or by tightening hasPermission itself, since hasPermission is shared by callers that legitimately pass multiple scopes.

items.defectStatement: At lines 1077-1078, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a silent no-op whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`. Because `evt.destinationCalendar` is built at lines 1063-1067 as `eventType.destinationCalendar ? [...] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [...] : null`, a COLLECTIVE team booking where neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar leaves it `null`, so the collective team members' destination calendars collected in `teamDestinationCalendars` are never appended and those hosts receive no calendar entry for the booking.
obligations: For a COLLECTIVE team event, the team members' destination calendars (teamDestinationCalendars) must end up in evt.destinationCalendar even when neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar is set (the previously-null case).

When evt.destinationCalendar already holds an entry (event type or organizer), that entry must be preserved and the team members' calendars appended to it; the existing append/order semantics must not regress.
Behavior for non-team and non-COLLECTIVE (e.g. ROUND_ROBIN) events must be unchanged: the teamDestinationCalendars push must not run and evt.destinationCalendar must stay as constructed.

The resulting value must remain a valid DestinationCalendar[] (or null) for the type, and must not break the downstream consumer at ~line 1871 that guards on `evt.destinationCalendar && evt.destinationCalendar.length > 0`.
items.notes: Several fixes are valid: `evt.destinationCalendar = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` before pushing, assigning `[...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`, or defaulting the field to `[]` in the object literal. Creating a non-null empty array in the no-team case is acceptable since the downstream booking create already tests `.length > 0`. The finding's 'hosts are not invited' is a slight overstatement of mechanism: what is actually dropped is the team members' destination calendars (so their calendars are not written / invites not generated); the core claim that the push silently does nothing on null is accurate and matches the shown code.

items.defectStatement: In ClientPermissionsV2.canView(ClientModel), the first branch calls the no-argument global canView(), which returns true whenever a realm-wide/all-clients VIEW (or realm VIEW_CLIENTS/MANAGE_CLIENTS role) grant exists, so a client-specific resource with an explicit denial is never evaluated and the denied client is authorized; the per-client evaluation in hasPermission(client, VIEW) is only reached when the global check is false.
obligations: canView(client) must not return true merely because a global/all-clients VIEW permission is granted when the concrete client has its own resource/policies that deny the request; the concrete client must be evaluated (e.g. via hasPermission(client, VIEW) and/or canConfigure(client)) rather than being short-circuited by a global hasPermission(VIEW) check.

Preserved: a user who can configure/manage the specific client (canConfigure(client) -> canManage(client) -> hasPermission(client, MANAGE)) still views that client, and realm-role grants (VIEW_CLIENTS/MANAGE_CLIENTS, i.e. canViewClientDefault() and the MANAGE_CLIENTS check in canManage(client)) must still grant view so existing admins are not locked out.

The method must keep its signature and boolean-only, non-throwing behavior, and must remain safe when the realm resource server is null or no client/all-clients resource exists (return false rather than NPE).

Clients with no individual policies must remain viewable by an admin holding an all-clients VIEW grant (the fallback to the CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE resource in hasPermission(client, scope) is the intended path for that case).
items.notes: hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) already implements the intended precedence: it looks up the client's own resource first and only falls back to the all-clients resource when the client has no policies, so removing/guarding the global canView() call is a sufficient fix here. A valid minimal fix is `if (canViewClientDefault() || canConfigure(client) || hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)) return true;` (or equivalent reordering); the exact form is not prescribed. The finding's second half (ClientsResource.getClients() using a global listing shortcut) is in a different file and outside the cited lines 78-79, so a replacement for these lines should not be faulted for not addressing it.

items.defectStatement: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members (lines 71-75), each supplied username is passed to group.add without checking whether the user is already a group member or whether the same username appears more than once in the request. If group.add inserts a GroupUser join row, duplicate/existing memberships can violate the (group_id, user_id) uniqueness constraint and fail instead of succeeding idempotently; because the loop is not transactional, a mid-loop failure can also leave partial membership.
obligations: Duplicate usernames within one request, and usernames already belonging to the group, must be no-ops rather than errors, and the request must still return the normal success response when the remaining additions succeed.
Unknown usernames must continue to be silently ignored via User.find_by_username, and automatic groups must still be rejected before any membership change with can_not_modify_automatic (422).
All new memberships added by one request must be atomic: if processing or persistence fails partway, newly added memberships from that request must not remain persisted.
Existing response behavior must be preserved: successful additions render success_json, and a group.save failure renders render_json_error(group).
items.notes: The finding is valid only assuming Group#add does not itself deduplicate; the shown controller does no such check. A correct fix can prefilter with group.user_ids/users.exists?/find_or_create_by, or otherwise make the insert idempotent, and can wrap the loop and any persistence/save step in one transaction. The exact duplicate exception may be DB-specific (e.g. ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique or another constraint error), so the grader should not require one exception class. Whitespace trimming of usernames is not part of this finding.

items.defectStatement: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() populates and returns the raw V2 authorization resource IDs (which equal the group ID, per resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) and the GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE resources) as the set of groups with view permission. This set is consumed by the JPA user search/count filtering (JpaUserProvider's groupsWithPermissionsSubquery), which still matches the legacy resource name 'group.resource.<groupId>'; because V2 resources carry only the bare group ID, the filter matches nothing, so users who are members only of V2-permissioned groups are never returned or counted.
obligations: Users who are members of a group for which the admin holds VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS (as evaluated by hasPermission) must be included in the JPA-backed user search/count results; users whose only group memberships lack those permissions must remain excluded.

The set returned by getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() (or the consumer's matching logic) must use a resource-name form that the JPA subquery actually matches: either the legacy 'group.resource.<groupId>' convention or a V2-aware comparison against bare group IDs.
Existing short-circuits must be preserved: empty set when root.users().canView(), when !root.isAdminSameRealm(), and when the resource server is null.
Only groups whose evaluated scopes include VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS may be included in the returned set; no other groups may be added.
items.notes: The cited line 127 (`return granted;`) is where the value is emitted, but the mismatched value is added at line 123 (`granted.add(groupResource.getId())`); a fix at either line, or a change in JpaUserProvider's groupsWithPermissionsSubquery to accept V2 naming, can satisfy the obligations. Do not require a specific prefix if the JPA contract is changed instead. Other valid fix: keep raw IDs here and update the subquery comparison. The core assertion — the returned IDs are bare group IDs while the downstream filter expects 'group.resource.<id>' — matches the shown code (findByName(server, groupId) and GROUP_RESOURCE_TYPE resources).

items.defectStatement: In checkIfIsAvailable, the `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` early return at lines 133-135 short-circuits before the final `busy.every(...)` overlap check, so any slot falling inside a date override is reported available even when the host already has a conflicting booking (or the slot is otherwise busy).
obligations: A slot that lies within a matching date override and also overlaps an entry in `busy` must return false (busy-conflict detection must run for override days just as for normal days).

A slot within a date override must still be accepted when it is not blocked by busy time, including slots that fall outside the host's normal working hours (a date override replaces working hours, so the working-hours rejection must not be applied to override-matched slots).
Slots not covered by a date override must keep their existing behavior: outside-working-hours slots return false and busy-overlap logic is unchanged.
Slots on an override date but outside the override's [start, end] range must keep returning false.
items.notes: Do not just delete lines 133-135: that would let the workingHours block reject override slots that intentionally sit outside normal working hours (regression). A valid fix either (a) guards only the workingHours check with `if (!dateOverrideExist && ...)`, or (b) restructures so the busy/overlap check is the unconditional final step. Busy checks at lines 153-180 must remain the returning expression. The earlier `currentSeats` early return at lines 95-97 is separate pre-existing behavior and out of scope.

items.defectStatement: In updateEvent (lines 254-256), the fallback branch calls event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) while externalCalendarId is falsy in that branch, so the predicate can never match a real calendar and the expression resolves to undefined; the Google events.update call then runs with an undefined calendarId, which the API treats as 'primary' instead of the intended host destination calendar.
obligations: When externalCalendarId is truthy, selectedCalendar must still be exactly externalCalendarId (existing behavior preserved).

When externalCalendarId is falsy, selectedCalendar must resolve to the host's destination calendar external id (e.g. mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId, the first entry of event.destinationCalendar), and must not be derived from a find() that compares cal.externalId against the falsy externalCalendarId.
The resolved selectedCalendar must be what is passed as calendarId in both calendar.events.update and the follow-up calendar.events.patch inside the callback, so the patch targets the same calendar.
No new exceptions or rejected promises may be introduced when event.destinationCalendar is absent or empty; the function must still proceed to the update call.
items.notes: The finding's claim of a strict regression from the pre-diff `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` is questionable: destinationCalendar is an array (see the createEvent change in the same diff), so that old expression also yielded undefined. Either way, the fallback must resolve to a real destination-calendar external id rather than undefined/'primary'. Any implementation that yields the main host destination calendar's externalId as fallback is acceptable; using mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId is the intended one. Note the identical faulty find pattern was also introduced in deleteEvent (lines ~315-317), but only lines 254-256 are cited and should be judged here.

items.defectStatement: After destructuring `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, the element is `undefined` whenever the array is null, undefined, or empty; the following line dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`, so a Meet-location event with no host destination calendar throws a TypeError and aborts event creation. The diff comment confirms callers now pass an array (possibly empty), so this is reachable.
obligations: With `evt.location === MeetLocationType` and `evt.destinationCalendar` null, undefined, or an empty array, the code must not throw; it should fall back to `integrations:daily` (matching the prior null-safe behavior where `undefined !== "google_calendar"`).
When the first destination calendar's `integration` is `"google_calendar"`, the Meet location must be preserved (no daily override).
When the first destination calendar's `integration` is any other value, the Meet location must fall back to `integrations:daily`.
Non-Meet locations must continue to bypass this block entirely (no override, no throw).
items.notes: Only lines 118-119 are cited. Valid fixes include optional chaining on the destructured element, `evt.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.integration`, or an explicit guard/early check; grader should accept any that yield the fallback semantics above. Do not conflate with the later destinationCalendar array changes in createAllCalendarEvents/updateAllCalendarEvents.

items.defectStatement: In scheduleEmailReminders.ts lines 53-77, the single try/catch wraps the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop, so if `client.request` throws for any one reminder (e.g. SendGrid 4xx on an already-sent/already-cancelled batch_id), the loop aborts immediately: remaining reminders are neither cancelled at SendGrid nor deleted from the DB, and the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` promises already pushed at line 72 are never awaited because `await Promise.all(...)` at line 74 is skipped. Those remaining reminders belong to cancelled/rescheduled bookings, so they can still be scheduled and sent, reproducing the bug this code is meant to fix.
obligations: A failure cancelling/scheduling one reminder must not stop the remaining `remindersToCancel` entries from being processed; every reminder in the loop must be attempted regardless of earlier per-item errors.
The collected Prisma delete operations must still be awaited/executed even when one or more SendGrid cancel requests fail (i.e. the DB cleanup must not be skipped due to a network error).

The existing error-logging behavior must be preserved (errors are caught and logged, not thrown out of this block); the handler must continue to the downstream `unscheduledReminders` step and still return a response rather than failing the whole request.

Behavior for the failure case itself must remain sane: a reminder whose SendGrid cancel failed must be handled consistently (either still deleted from the DB or intentionally skipped), without leaving the loop in an aborted state.
items.notes: Finding is accurate as stated against the cited lines. Both of these are valid fix shapes and should be accepted: (a) move try/catch inside the loop and keep the shared `Promise.all` for the deletes (ideally awaited independently of the per-item request), or (b) wrap each iteration in its own async task and use `Promise.allSettled`. Whether a reminder is deleted from the DB when its SendGrid cancel failed is a deliberate design choice, not mandated; graders should accept either deleting anyway (best-effort cleanup) or skipping that reminder's delete, as long as the loop keeps going and the other deletes are awaited. Do not require that the whole handler throw on error — swallowing/logging per item is the intended fix. Note the delete is only pushed after the await completes, so a throwing request means no delete promise exists for that reminder.

items.defectStatement: In the new `else` branch (lines 178-186), any falsy return from `twilio.scheduleSMS` is treated as a send failure and increments `retryCount`. But `scheduleSMS` returns `undefined` on a non-error path when SMS sending is locked (`isLockedForSMSSending`), so a temporary lock is counted as a failure and the reminder is permanently deleted by the top-of-file `deleteMany` once `retryCount > 1`, silently dropping a valid reminder that should be retried after the lock is lifted.
obligations: A reminder whose send was skipped because SMS sending is locked must not have its retryCount incremented (and must not be marked scheduled).
Genuine send errors must still increment retryCount (the existing catch-block increment behavior is preserved), so real failures are retried and eventually dropped.
Successfully scheduled SMS reminders must still be updated with scheduled: true and the returned referenceId.
Locked/skipped reminders must remain unscheduled in the DB so a later cron run retries them rather than deleting them.
items.notes: The finding is accurate assuming scheduleSMS returns undefined for the lock path as described. Distinct return values for locked vs. failed sends, or checking the lock before calling scheduleSMS, are both valid fixes; the grader should accept any approach that stops counting the locked/skipped case as a failure. Trap: do not simply remove the else branch if scheduleSMS can also return falsy for genuine failures — the catch block only covers thrown errors. Out of scope but worth knowing: the new `deleteMany` OR clause with `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` applies to all reminders regardless of method or scheduled date, and retryCount may be null in the DB.

items.defectStatement: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` unconditionally sets `data.refresh_token = 'refresh_token'` whenever the parsed (and possibly provider-optional) `refresh_token` is absent. In the non-sharing branch this value flows into the caller's credential merge (e.g. office365calendar spreads `tokenResponse.data` over stored `o365AuthCredentials`), replacing a still-valid stored refresh token with the literal `"refresh_token"` and breaking subsequent refreshes; the placeholder is only meaningful for the credential-sharing/sync path that parses with `minimumTokenResponseSchema`.
obligations: In the default/non-sharing branch, absence of `refresh_token` in the provider response must not result in the parsed data carrying the literal `"refresh_token"` in a way that overwrites a caller's existing valid refresh token.
If the credential-sharing/sync path still needs a `refresh_token` present in the returned data, that behavior must be retained for that path.
The failure behavior must be preserved: when the chosen schema's `safeParse` fails, throw `Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")`.
The function must continue to return the safeParse-shaped result (with `success` and `data`) so existing callers that read `tokenResponse.data` keep working.
items.notes: Finding is accurate as written. Multiple valid fixes: gate injection behind a caller-supplied flag, only apply it when the `minimumTokenResponseSchema` branch was used, or move placeholder handling into the sharing/sync caller. Trap: blindly deleting the injection may break the credential-sync path that expects a `refresh_token` field; a correct fix keeps that path working. A grader should verify no existing caller of the non-sharing branch has its stored refresh token clobbered.

items.defectStatement: In the organization create payload (line 151), the condition guarding the direct `slug` field was changed from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`, inverting the behavior: the slug is now written directly on the organization whenever team billing IS enabled (instead of going through the requestedSlug/payment flow), and is never written at all when billing is disabled. The metadata `requestedSlug` line (153) was rewritten from `&&` to a ternary but is behavior-equivalent (`...false` is a no-op), so only the slug line is actually broken.
obligations: When IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is false, the organization create data must still include the `slug` field set to the input slug.
When IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, the organization create data must NOT include a direct `slug` field (the slug is handled via the metadata `requestedSlug`/billing flow).
The metadata `requestedSlug` behavior must be preserved: it is set only when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true.
All other organization fields (name, metadata.isOrganization, isOrganizationVerified, isOrganizationConfigured, orgAutoAcceptEmail) must remain unchanged.
items.notes: Only cited line 151 is defective; line 153's `&&` -> ternary rewrite is semantically equivalent and does not need reverting (though restoring `&&` would also be acceptable). Any fix that makes the slug field conditional on `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is valid, e.g. `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` or the original `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`.

items.defectStatement: In checkIfIsAvailable (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts, lines 114-116), the full-day date-override check compares two freshly constructed Dayjs objects with `===`, i.e. JavaScript reference equality, which is always false for distinct objects. Consequently an override whose start and end denote the same instant (a full-day unavailable override) is never detected by this branch, the surrounding `dateOverrides.find(...)` callback falls through to the range checks, and the slot is treated as available instead of being excluded.
obligations: The full-day branch must compare the offset-adjusted start and end as values (instant/date equality), not by object reference, so it evaluates true when start and end represent the same moment.

When that equality holds for an override on the slot's day, the callback must report a match so the enclosing `if (dateOverrides.find(...))` causes checkIfIsAvailable to return false (slot excluded), matching the intent of the existing comment 'slot is not within the date override'.

Behavior must be preserved for all other cases: same-day overrides with start < end still flow through the existing isBefore/isSame/isAfter range checks unchanged, and an override day that matches but contains the slot must still leave dateOverrideExist true and the function returning true.

The utcOffset applied to both endpoints must remain consistent with the rest of the block (both sides shifted by the same offset); the fix must not alter the offset computation or the surrounding find/return structure.
items.notes: Valid alternatives: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset,'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset,'minutes'))`, or comparing `date.start`/`date.end` timestamps (e.g. `.valueOf()`/`getTime()`) or `isSame` on unshifted dates — since both sides receive the identical offset, any instant-equality check is equivalent. Trap: `dayjs(...) === dayjs(...)` is always false here; also don't 'fix' it by comparing because the objects are separate. Scope is only lines 114-116; do not touch the neighboring isBefore/isSame/isAfter conditions.

items.defectStatement: In addGuestsHandler, blacklistedGuestEmails entries are lowercased but each guest is compared as-is via blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest). As a result, a blocked address such as Blocked@Example.com or a plus-address alias such as blocked+foo@example.com bypasses the blacklist and is added as an attendee.
obligations: Guest-to-blacklist comparison must be case-insensitive: Blocked@Example.com must be treated the same as blocked@example.com.
Guest-to-blacklist comparison must use base-email normalization so a plus alias (e.g. blocked+anything@example.com) matches a blacklisted base address (e.g. blocked@example.com).
Non-blacklisted guests must still be added, and the email persisted via guestsFullDetails/createMany must remain the original guest string, not a normalized or lowercased version.

Existing filtering behavior must be preserved: guests already present as attendees are still excluded, and when no guests remain uniqueGuests the handler still throws BAD_REQUEST with emails_must_be_unique_valid.
items.notes: The finding is accurate. The reference to base-email normalization in handleNewBooking is contextual; this handler currently contains no such normalization. Valid fixes include normalizing the guest with extractBaseEmail(guest).toLowerCase() before the blacklist comparison, or normalizing both guest and blacklist entries with extractBaseEmail(...).toLowerCase(); lowercasing only fixes the case bypass and not the plus-alias bypass. Do not change the guest value used later in guestsFullDetails/createMany; normalization is only for comparison. The existing attendee duplicate check guest === attendee.email is a separate comparison and is not required by this finding to change. Blacklisted guests are currently silently filtered out rather than rejected; preserve that flow (an all-filtered list then triggers the existing BAD_REQUEST).

items.defectStatement: In the recurring-series branch (lines 449-461), the deletion loop iterates over every one of bookingToDelete.user.credentials and, for each credential, deletes only the first calendar reference found in each updatedBooking (lines 454-457), ignoring that reference's own credentialId. With multiple calendar references (e.g. collective bookings with co-host calendars), this leaves the other references' events undeleted, deletes the same first event repeatedly through unrelated calendar credentials, and re-runs the whole promise block once for every outer calendar reference (line 423).
obligations: Each calendar reference of each remaining occurrence in updatedBookings must be deleted using the credential identified by that reference's credentialId (resolved from bookingToDelete.user.credentials or the prisma DB fallback), not by looping every calendar credential over one chosen reference.
All calendar references per occurrence must be processed, not just the first one returned by find.
A given event (integer uid/externalCalendarId pair) for an occurrence must be deleted at most once; neither iterating credentials nor the outer per-reference loop may cause duplicate deletions.

Preserve existing behavior outside this branch: single-event deletion for non-recurring bookings, the credentialId-less pre-refactor fallback (lines 473-482), apiDeletes accumulation, and the Promise.all error logging.
items.notes: Alternative valid fixes include restructuring the allRemainingBookings branch to iterate updatedBookings and their calendar refs, resolving each ref's credential (making the outer bookingCalendarReference loop redundant for this branch). The grader should accept any structure that deletes each occurrence's refs once with the matching credential. Note evt is passed through to deleteEvent. The outer resolved calendarCredential/calendar (lines 442-443) is unused inside the branch because the inner `const calendar` shadows it — that shadowing/ignoring is central to the defect. The finding is accurate; per-occurrence credential resolution may need the DB fallback because co-host credentials are not present in bookingToDelete.user.credentials.

items.defectStatement: In referencesToCreate (line 170), the non-calendar (video) branch of credentialId was changed from the previous `result.credentialId` to a hard-coded `undefined`. As a result, video booking references (e.g. Cal Video / Daily) no longer persist the credential id that created them, so that integration can no longer be located for later update/delete.
obligations: For non-calendar results, credentialId must be derived from the result (result.credentialId), not hard-coded to undefined — restoring the pre-change behavior.
For calendar results, credentialId must remain sourced from result.credentialId, matching the intent of the diff (previously evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId).
The externalCalendarId and other reference fields (type, uid, meetingId, meetingPassword, meetingUrl) must retain their current behavior for both branches.
The returned object must still satisfy the reference type expected by referencesToCreate (credentialId type-compatible), and must not introduce a throw for video results whose credentialId is absent.
items.notes: The finding's defect is accurate: the diff moved the non-calendar branch from result.credentialId to undefined. The finding's proposed 'HOW' expression `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : result.credentialId` is redundant (both branches equal) and reduces to plain `result.credentialId`; that, or `result.credentialId ?? undefined` (consistent with updateLocation line 209), are both valid fixes. Since calendar now also sources from result.credentialId, a single unconditional `result.credentialId` preserves all behavior; a grader should accept either form.

items.defectStatement: In addGuestsHandler, isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, which is only true when the user is BOTH a team admin and a team owner. A team admin who is not an owner (and vice versa) fails this check and, unless they are the organizer or an attendee, is rejected with FORBIDDEN. Authorization should be satisfied by either role, i.e. `||`.
obligations: The permission flag must be true when the user is a team admin OR a team owner of the booking's event-type team (booking.eventType?.teamId).

The subsequent guard must remain intact: throw TRPCError FORBIDDEN 'you_do_not_have_permission' when the flag is false AND the user is neither the organizer (booking.userId === user.id) nor an attendee.
The organizer and attendee authorization paths must be preserved unchanged, including the fallback `booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0`.
Bookings not tied to a team (teamId missing/0) must continue to deny non-organizer, non-attendee users rather than accidentally authorizing them.
items.notes: The finding is accurate; `||` (or equivalent short-circuit/conditional logic) is the correct operator. Any implementation that makes either role sufficient is acceptable. Note that the two async checks are independent lookups, so switching to `||` does not change side effects. Do not weaken the organizer/attendee fallback logic or the error code/message.

items.defectStatement: In the working-hours block (lines 138-151), `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` (line 142) so it always equals `start` and the `end > workingHour.endTime` bound never fires, letting a slot that overruns working hours through. Additionally the block uses `workingHours.find(...)` whose callback returns `true` for any day-matching entry that does not contain the slot, so with multiple entries on the same day (e.g. 9-12 and 13-17) a slot inside one entry is rejected because another entry does not contain it.
obligations: `end` must be the slot's end in minutes derived from `slotEndTime` (e.g. `slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute()`), so a slot whose end exceeds `workingHour.endTime` is treated as outside working hours.

A slot that is fully contained (start >= workingHour.startTime && end <= workingHour.endTime) in at least one working-hours entry for the slot's day must NOT be rejected by this block; it must fall through to the busy check, even when other same-day entries do not contain it.
A slot on a day that has working-hours entries, where no entry contains the whole slot, must still `return false` (outside working hours) as before.
Preserve surrounding behavior: no working-hours entry for that day does not by itself reject here, and the preceding date-override logic and the following `busy.every(...)` check are unchanged.
items.notes: Multiple valid fixes exist: e.g. `if (!workingHours.some(wh => wh.days.includes(day) && start >= wh.startTime && end <= wh.endTime) && workingHours.some(wh => wh.days.includes(day)))` or equivalent some-containment logic. The finding's phrasing 'reject only if no entry on that day contains the whole slot' is slightly ambiguous about days with zero entries; preserving the original behavior (zero entries for the day falls through rather than rejecting) satisfies obligation 4. Note `slotEndTime` is UTC-based (line 99); an end-minute value can still be lower than start for slots crossing midnight — that pre-existing limitation is out of scope for grading.

items.defectStatement: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() (GroupPermissionsV2.java lines 121-125), both the identifier passed to hasPermission() and the value added to the returned set come from groupResource.getId(), which is the internal authorization Resource UUID, not the group id. Since resources of type GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE are named with the group id and hasPermission() resolves them via resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId), passing the UUID makes findByName return null, so the check silently falls back to the all-groups resource, and the set handed back to callers (used for UserModel.GROUPS filtering) contains UUIDs that match no group, so no users are returned.
obligations: The set returned by getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() must contain group ids (i.e., the group resource's name), not Resource UUIDs.

The permission check for each group resource must be performed against that group's own resource (the identifier passed to hasPermission() must resolve via findByName to the same resource being iterated), not the all-groups fallback.

The existing scopes checked (VIEW_MEMBERS and MANAGE_MEMBERS) and the existing early-return behavior (empty set when the admin can view users, is not same-realm, or has no resource server) must be preserved.
Only resources of type AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE that pass the permission check should be added to the result.
items.notes: The finding correctly identifies the bug; the fix for both offending uses (the hasPermission() argument and granted.add()) must be consistent — changing only one leaves the bug (mismatched id in the check or UUIDs in the result). Passing groupResource.getName() is the natural fix, but any approach yielding the group id equivalent works. Do not modify hasPermission()'s findByName lookup, which relies on resources being named by group id; also note findByName is used elsewhere (e.g., canViewMembers) with group.getId(), which is correct there because Resource is named by group id.

items.defectStatement: In Office365CalendarService.createEvent, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` unconditionally picks the first entry of the destinationCalendar array. For collective/team bookings `event.destinationCalendar` can contain one entry per connected host credential, so when CalendarManager invokes this service with a co-host's credential the POST is built from the organiser's (or another host's) `externalId` while being authenticated with the co-host's token, so the event is written to the wrong calendar or Graph rejects it. The method ignores the credentialId that CalendarManager passes to select the matching destination.
obligations: createEvent must choose the destinationCalendar entry whose credentialId corresponds to the credential invoking this call (i.e. accept/use the credentialId argument supplied by CalendarManager) rather than taking index 0 of event.destinationCalendar.

When no destinationCalendar entry matches that credential (single-credential bookings, empty/undefined destinationCalendar), the previous behaviour must be preserved: fall back gracefully (e.g. the prior first-entry or `/me/calendar/events` default) without throwing.

The URL construction must still be `/me/calendars/{externalId}/events` when an externalId is selected, and `/me/calendar/events` otherwise; POST body, error handling and the returned `{ ...responseJson, iCalUID: responseJson.iCalUId }` shape must stay unchanged.
The method signature must stay compatible with its callers/interface (event plus the credential id), and updateEvent/deleteEvent/getAvailability must not be altered.
items.notes: Valid alternative fixes exist and should be accepted: filtering with `.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)` (or `.filter(...)[0]`), or matching against the credential the instance was constructed with (this.credentials id) if the constructor stores it — both satisfy the obligations. Note the cited diff already repaired an earlier bug where `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (an array, so always undefined) forced every call to `/me/calendar/events`; the fix must not reintroduce that. The finding's mechanism is accurate; only caution is that behaviour when no matching entry exists is not specified by the finding and should default to the pre-existing fallback rather than an error.

items.defectStatement: In the catch block (lines 189-197) the retry counter is written as `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, using a value read earlier when the reminder list was fetched. This is a non-atomic read-modify-write, so concurrent or overlapping failures for the same reminder can both compute the same value and undercount retries, defeating the retry-limit/count logic added in the diff.
obligations: The catch-block update must increment retryCount atomically against the stored row value (e.g. Prisma `{ increment: 1 }`) instead of writing `reminder.retryCount + 1` computed from the in-memory reminder.
The update must still target the failing reminder by its id so only that row's retryCount changes.
Existing catch behavior must be preserved: the original scheduling error is still logged, and control flow after the catch (response handling) is unchanged.
The successful-scheduling path (setting `scheduled: true` and `referenceId`) must not be altered by the fix.
items.notes: The else branch (lines 178-187) contains the identical non-atomic pattern; the finding cites only the catch block, but a fix that also converts the else branch is valid and arguably desirable for consistency. An alternative valid fix is re-reading the current retryCount before writing, but a true atomic increment is the robust choice and should be accepted. Note the diff's cleanup filter uses `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` and the reminder select now includes retryCount; those are out of scope for this finding.

items.defectStatement: In checkIfIsAvailable, the dateOverrides.find callback sets dateOverrideExist as a side effect and returns truthy when a slot is outside a given override. When multiple date overrides fall on the same day, a slot that lies inside one override but outside another causes find to return the outside override, so the function incorrectly returns false (slot unavailable) even though the slot is covered by the first override.
obligations: If multiple date overrides match the slot's day, the function must return available (true) when the slot falls within at least one of them, regardless of other same-day overrides.
If date overrides match the slot's day but the slot falls outside every same-day override, the function must return unavailable (false).
If no date override matches the slot's day, the function must fall through to the working-hours and busy-time checks (preserve existing behavior).
The per-override containment test must be independent of iteration order or short-circuiting; a side-effect flag must not conflate the results of different overrides.
items.notes: The finding is accurate. The zero-length override case (start === end) intentionally marks the day unavailable and should be preserved. Unrelated bugs in the same function (e.g., working-hours end calculation, utcOffset sign) are out of scope.

items.defectStatement: In handleCancelBooking.ts lines 444-461 the recurring bulk-cancel block (iterating all of bookingToDelete.user.credentials and all updatedBookings to delete their calendar events) was moved inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop, but it does not use the loop variable `reference` at all. With multiple calendar references, the identical set of deleteEvent calls is issued once per reference, so the same events are deleted N times and the duplicate attempts error/log noise.
obligations: For a recurring cancellation with allRemainingBookings (recurringEvent && recurringEventId && allRemainingBookings), the bulk delete over updatedBookings x all calendar credentials must be performed exactly once per handler invocation, regardless of how many calendar references the booking has.

Non-recurring behavior per reference must be preserved: each calendar reference is deleted through its own credential (looked up by credentialId, falling back to a DB lookup when not found in user.credentials), and references without a credentialId still fall back to the legacy path of deleting via every calendar credential.

The recurring bulk-delete path must remain resilient: errors from the delete promises are caught and logged rather than aborting the handler (existing try/catch around Promise.all semantics preserved).

When the recurring/allRemainingBookings condition does not hold, each reference must still result in a single deleteEvent call (the else branch), i.e. the fix must not drop or duplicate the ordinary per-reference deletion.
items.notes: The cited block is genuinely independent of `reference`, so the duplication diagnosis is accurate. The finding's second complaint (other hosts' events not deleted through their own credentials) is a pre-existing limitation of this block, not introduced by the diff, and a grader should not require fixing it; a fix that only deduplicates the bulk run is sufficient. Valid fixes include hoisting the recurring block above/after the reference loop (guarded so ordinary per-reference deletes are still not skipped in the recurring case) or otherwise ensuring a single execution; several structures are acceptable.

items.defectStatement: In createEvent, the insert call resolves the target calendar as `selectedCalendar || "primary"` (line 154), but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` call in the insert callback passes the raw `selectedCalendar` as `calendarId` (line 168). Because `selectedCalendar` is derived from `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find(...)?.externalId`, it is `undefined` whenever destinationCalendar is empty or no entry matches the credentialId — so the insert succeeds on "primary" while the conference-data/hangout-link patch is issued with an undefined calendarId and fails (or is sent as an invalid `calendars/undefined/...` request) instead of patching the just-inserted event.
obligations: The calendarId used in the `calendar.events.patch` call inside the insert callback must resolve to the same value used by `calendar.events.insert` for the same invocation.
When `selectedCalendar` (externalId of the destinationCalendar entry matching `credentialId`) is undefined/absent, the patch must fall back to "primary" rather than passing undefined.
When a matching destinationCalendar entry exists, the patch must still target that entry's externalId (behavior for the configured-calendar case must be preserved).

Whether the fix introduces one resolved local variable or repeats the `|| "primary"` fallback inline, both insert and patch must stay in sync; no other behavior of createEvent (payload, attendees, resolution, return value) should change.
items.notes: The cited range (145-154) shows the resolution and insert; the actual defect line is 168 in the same method (patch uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar`). A grader should accept any fix that makes patch use the same resolved id, e.g. `const calendarId = selectedCalendar || "primary"` used in both calls, or `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"` at line 168. Slight overstatement in the finding: passing an undefined calendarId does not silently target the *wrong* calendar — it produces an invalid request that fails; the practical failure (hangout link never patched onto the event) is as described. Note also that this patch call is not awaited and its error is not handled, but that pre-existing behavior is out of scope for this fix.

items.defectStatement: In the catch block at packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts lines 189-197, the awaited prisma.workflowReminder.update that increments retryCount is not itself guarded. If that update rejects (e.g. the reminder row was already removed by the deleteMany/batch cleanup or a concurrent run, or a transient DB error occurs), the exception is thrown out of the catch block, aborts the surrounding for loop so remaining reminders are never processed, and propagates out of the handler (the console.log at line 198 is skipped). The finding is accurate as written.
obligations: A failure of the retryCount persistence update inside the catch block must not terminate the for loop: all remaining unscheduled reminders in the batch must still be iterated.
A failure of that update must not propagate out of the handler after the loop; the endpoint should still reach the res.status(200).json({ message: "SMS scheduled" }) response as before.
The original scheduling error must still be logged (the console.log of `error`) even when the retryCount update fails.

When the retryCount update succeeds, the existing behavior of incrementing retryCount (= reminder.retryCount + 1) for the failed reminder must be preserved; unrelated scheduling/success paths (lines 158-188) must remain unchanged.
items.notes: Both a nested try/catch around the update and simply moving the console.log before the update are valid fixes; the latter still throws on update failure but at least logs, so a grader should not require one specific shape — only that the loop/handler survivability and logging obligations above hold. Trap: because the console.log currently follows the update, a fix that only reorders the log without swallowing the error would still abort the loop, so accepting it depends on whether the grader treats 'must not abort the loop' as mandatory; it is stated as mandatory here. The finding's mention of 'record already deleted' is plausible: the same handler's deleteMany (diff, lines 28-38) can remove rows with retryCount > 1, and retryCount is now selected (diff, lines 53-58) so reminder.retryCount is defined. The parallel update at lines 179-186 sits inside the try and is not separately at issue.

items.defectStatement: In checkIfIsAvailable's working-hours guard (slots.ts lines 138-151), the callback computes `end` as a copy of `start` and uses `workingHours.find` to reject when any single matching weekday range fails to contain the slot. A split schedule with multiple ranges on the same day therefore rejects slots that fall inside one of the ranges, and the slot's actual end time is never validated against the range end.
obligations: Reject a slot via the working-hours guard only when no applicable workingHours entry contains the full slot interval, where applicable means the entry's days include the slot's weekday and start >= entry.startTime and slot end <= entry.endTime.
Use the actual slot end time derived from slotEndTime when comparing against workingHour.endTime, not a duplicate of the slot start time.

Treat multiple workingHours entries for the same weekday as alternatives: a slot completely inside at least one applicable range must not be rejected because another applicable range does not contain it.

Preserve the other availability checks (currentSeats, dateOverrides, busy time logic, and final true return) and do not change behavior for slots that are not subject to the working-hours restriction.
items.notes: The finding correctly identifies the any-vs-some defect, but the shown code also has a second bug: `end` is set equal to `start`, so slot end is never checked. A fix must address both.
