The suggested `!workingHours.some(...)` shape is valid for non-empty arrays, but if empty workingHours is meant to mean “no working-hours restriction,” a length guard is needed; otherwise `!workingHours.some(...)` rejects all slots when the array is empty.

items.defectStatement: In deleteScheduledSMSReminder (lines 177-186) the prisma.workflowReminder.delete for reminderId is placed inside the same try block immediately after await twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId), so any Twilio failure (or a thrown cancelSMS) causes the delete to be skipped entirely and the workflowReminder row is left in the DB. Note: the finding's claim that 'previously the caller deleted the reminder row independently' is contradicted by the FileDiff — the old version issued no prisma delete at all, so this is a newly introduced coupling rather than a regression of prior independent deletion, but the concrete risk (stale scheduled row after a failed cancel) is still real.
obligations: When referenceId is null, the function must still attempt to delete the workflowReminder row with the given reminderId (no Twilio call required, delete must not be skipped for that reason).
A thrown/failed twilio.cancelSMS must not prevent the workflowReminder row from being deleted (or otherwise marked/handled so the reminder will not still be sent).
The function must keep its current error-handling contract: it does not rethrow, and errors are logged/caught so callers are not broken.
The delete must target the reminder row identified by reminderId (callers unaffected by the added reminderId parameter).
items.notes: Several fixes are valid: move the prisma delete outside/before the Twilio try, wrap the delete in its own try, or use a finally. A grader should accept deleting before the Twilio call, after it in a separate try, or in a finally, as long as the row is removed regardless of Twilio outcome. Do not require marking-cancelled/retry — that is one alternative, not the only correct behavior. Also flag if the fix drops the console.log error handling or reintroduces unconditioned cancelSMS call when referenceId is null.

items.defectStatement: In the override mapping, startTime/endTime are computed as `.hour()*60 + .minute()` on the timezone-shifted instant, which drops the calendar-day component. When the organizer-to-invitee shift pushes an override across midnight (e.g. a 20:00-23:00 override moved +6h lands at 02:00-05:00 the next day), the values wrap into 0-1439 and the override is placed at the wrong time of the invitee day (or, when the shifted range itself crosses midnight, yields endTime < startTime), so the generated slots are wrong or empty.
obligations: startTime and endTime must be minute offsets relative to the same day origin used by the other availability data and by buildSlots (startOfInviteeDay), computed from the timezone-converted instants, so a converted time that falls on the following day yields a value beyond 1440 (or negative) instead of wrapping modulo 24h; specifically, the hour()*60+minute() extraction must be gone.

The existing timezone conversion must be preserved: the offset derived from the organizer's override.timeZone vs the invitee's timeZone must still be applied, and an override in the same timezone (offset 0) must produce the same times as before.
For a shifted override whose interval crosses midnight, endTime must stay greater than startTime (no wrap-around), so the override still contributes a valid range.
userIds semantics must be unchanged: [] when override.userId is absent, [override.userId] otherwise.
items.notes: The finding is accurate; the cited lines are from the new (post-diff) code. Valid fixes include `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, 'minute').diff(startOfInviteeDay, 'minute')` or the finding's `.tz(timeZone).diff(startOfInviteeDay, 'minute')`; the grader should accept any expression that computes non-modulo offsets against the same day origin, and should not mandate a specific dayjs chain. Do not require values >= 1440 for ordinary same-day overrides (they must equal the old time-of-day values); only require no wrap for cross-midnight conversions. Downstream handling of offsets >= 1440 (chunk merge, splice, buildSlots day mapping) is outside these lines.

items.defectStatement: In CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx lines 42-50, deleteCacheMutation's onSuccess only fires the toast and the parent onSuccess?() callback; unlike disconnectMutation (lines 61-64) it never invalidates utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, so after a successful cache deletion the dropdown can keep rendering the stale cacheUpdatedAt (the 'cache_last_updated' display at lines 88-94) unless the parent happens to refetch on its own.
obligations: After a successful viewer.calendars.deleteCache call, the viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars query must be invalidated/refetched so the value passed in as the cacheUpdatedAt prop is updated.
Existing success behavior must be preserved: the 'cache_deleted_successfully' toast and the parent onSuccess?.() call still run on success, and the 'error_deleting_cache' toast still runs on error.
The disconnectMutation behavior (onSuccess callback + invalidate connectedCalendars and apps.integrations in onSettled) must remain unchanged.

Any invalidation added to deleteCacheMutation must be schedulable — note `utils` is declared at line 52, after the mutation at line 42; referencing it inside the mutation's callback body is fine at call time, but a fix that reads `utils` during render at that point would break.
items.notes: The finding is essentially correct: no invalidation exists in the cited onSuccess. It is slightly overstated in that the staleness only manifests if the parent does not refetch, and invalidation only helps if the parent renders cacheUpdatedAt from the connectedCalendars query; still, matching disconnectMutation's invalidation is the reasonable fix. Valid alternatives: invalidate inside deleteCacheMutation's onSuccess or onSettled (onSettled is what disconnectMutation uses), and both are acceptable. A fix that additionally invalidates viewer.apps.integrations is harmless but not required. Do not require a specific callback hook (onSuccess vs onSettled) as long as invalidate runs after a successful deletion.

items.defectStatement: Each entry of `appStore` is `import("./x")` evaluated directly in the object literal, so every app module's chunk/dependency graph is actually requested as soon as `@calcom/app-store` is evaluated; the dynamic-form syntax buys no laziness because the import expressions run at module init rather than per use. Any consumer of the lookup helpers consequently triggers loading of all calendars/video/payment apps.
obligations: Loading must be deferred: no app module may be fetched/evaluated merely by importing the appStore module; the import expression must only run when the specific key is requested at a use site.
The set of keys in `appStore` must be unchanged (same 28 app ids, including the commented `example` placeholder staying a comment) and the default export must remain the appStore object.

Every value must still be obtainable as a promise resolving to the same module namespace object as before (e.g. a zero-arg function returning `import("./x")`), so callers can await it and get the identical module shape; the async shape of lookups must not silently become a sync value.

The consuming lookup sites (getCalendar, getVideoAdapters, payment lookups) must be updated consistently so they await/invoke the entry rather than using the raw value — a fix that only changes this file and leaves consumers treating entries as promise-or-module would break at runtime with "is not a function".
items.notes: The finding's diagnosis is accurate as far as the cited lines go (browser/webpack: `import()` chunks are requested at evaluation time). Its `await appStore[key]?.()` sketch is one valid shape; an equivalent valid fix is a getter-based lazy map (Object.defineProperty with `get: () => import(...)`) or explicit per-app lazy accessor functions, so graders should not require thunk-call syntax specifically. Trap: reverting to static `import * as x` is NOT a valid fix — it re-introduces eager loading. Note the cited lines cover only the object literal; the required consumer-side call-site changes live outside this window, so a replacement limited to these lines can at most satisfy the definitional/typing half of the obligations.

items.defectStatement: Line 31 calls appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) without any error handling, so a request whose body is missing or has a wrong-typed userId/appSlug/keys makes Zod throw a ZodError that propagates out of the handler, producing an unhandled 500 instead of the intended 400 client-error response.
obligations: A request body that fails appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema (missing or wrong-typed userId/appSlug/keys, non-object/missing body) must result in an HTTP 400 JSON response and must not throw out of the handler.
Body validation must still occur before any DB lookups, decryption, or credential writes; no `reqBody.userId`/`appSlug`/`keys` access for an invalid body.
The existing 403 checks for disabled credential sharing and mismatched webhook secret must remain first, so unauthenticated/invalid-secret requests still get 403 rather than 400.

All existing success and not-found behavior must be preserved for valid bodies: same schema constraints (integer userId, string appSlug, string keys), 404 for missing user/app/app metadata, 200 credential update/create with the same response messages.
items.notes: Both `safeParse` + early `return res.status(400).json(...)` and wrapping `parse` in try/catch are valid fixes; grader should accept either, and any message/shape for the 400 is fine as long as status is 400. Do not require error details be surfaced. Overstated in the finding: there is no meaningful 'exception leak' — Next.js just yields a generic 500; the real defect is the wrong status code and unhandled throw. Trap: a fix that changes the schema to coerce types (e.g. z.coerce.number(), or accepting string userId) alters accepted inputs rather than just handling failures — acceptable only if it still returns 400 for genuinely invalid values, but it goes beyond the cited defect. Also out of scope for this finding (do not require fixing, though a fix may include it): the JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) on line 57 can itself throw on bad keys.

items.defectStatement: The date-override containment check in checkIfIsAvailable only marks a slot as outside the override when it is fully disjoint from it. For a 10:00-11:00 override, intervals that partially overlap (09:30-10:30, 10:30-11:30) and intervals starting exactly at the override end (11:00-12:00) are not flagged by the two `return true` branches, so the predicate returns falsy, `dateOverrideExist` stays true, and the function returns `true` (slot treated as available) even though the event does not fit inside the override. The check must instead reject any slot not fully contained in [overrideStart, overrideEnd].
obligations: When a non-zero-length date override exists on the slot's day, the function must return false (unavailable) for any slot whose event interval is not fully contained in the override window: reject slotStartTime < overrideStart, reject slotEndTime > overrideEnd, and reject any partial overlap on either edge.

A slot whose interval sits entirely inside the override (including the exact-boundary case slotStartTime == overrideStart and slotEndTime == overrideEnd) must still be treated as within the override, preserving current behavior for fully-contained slots.

The zero-length override case (start == end, i.e. an exclusion/day-off) must continue to make the slot unavailable, and when no matching override exists for the slot's day the code must still fall through to the working-hours and busy-time logic unchanged.
The existing timezone/utcOffset adjustment applied to date.start and date.end when forming the override bounds must be preserved.
items.notes: Finding is accurate as written. Several implementations are valid (e.g. invert to a positive containment check `if (slotStartTime.isBefore(start) || slotEndTime.isAfter(end)) return true;`, or keep the negative form and tighten both branches with isBefore/isAfter plus same-boundary handling). Preserve strict inequality semantics at the outer edges: slotStart == overrideStart and slotEnd == overrideEnd are inside; slotStart == overrideEnd is outside. Not part of this finding, but be aware line 114 compares two distinct Dayjs objects with `===` (always false), so the zero-length-override branch is effectively dead; a fix touching only lines 117-124 need not change that, but a grader should not treat it as introduced by the fix.

items.defectStatement: ZAddGuestsInputSchema validates each guest as an email but performs no uniqueness check across the `guests` array, so a client can submit the same email twice (e.g. ["a@x.com","a@x.com"]) and it passes validation. Downstream persistence that inserts one attendee row per array element (e.g. createMany) then writes duplicate attendee records for that booking; the file shown contains only the schema, so the handler's exact insert behavior is not visible here.
obligations: Input containing the same guest email more than once (as validated by the email check) must not be able to produce duplicate attendee records: either the schema rejects the whole payload with a validation error, or the duplicates are removed before insertion.

Non-duplicate input must still be accepted unchanged: bookingId remains a required number and every distinct guest string must still be validated by z.string().email(), so invalid emails are still rejected.
The exported name ZAddGuestsInputSchema and the inferred type TAddGuestsInputSchema must remain valid/usable — no change to the module's public surface.
An empty `guests` array must remain valid, and order/first-occurrence semantics of the guest list must not be otherwise altered.
items.notes: Both a rejecting .refine()/.superRefine() and a .transform() that dedupes are acceptable fixes; .transform() changes the inferred output type, so a grader should not require rejection specifically, only that no duplicate reaches the insert. Trap: 'A@x.com' vs 'a@x.com' is not caught by naive exact-match comparison (zod's .email() accepts both); case-insensitive normalization is a stronger fix but is not required by the finding, which is about exact duplicates. The finding's claim about createMany inserting duplicates is inferred from other code not shown in the cited window; if the handler or DB already dedupes/enforces a unique constraint, the defect is limited to the schema accepting redundant input rather than being a true duplicate-insert bug.

items.defectStatement: The reschedule flow at packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:553-567 uses `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)`, so the async callbacks' promises are never awaited. Calendar `deleteEvent` and `deleteMeeting` calls therefore run fire-and-forget: the reschedule email (line 570) and BOOKING_CANCELLED webhook (lines 598-618) are sent before the old calendar/video events are deleted, and any rejection from these deletions is unobserved.
obligations: The reschedule mutation must await completion of all calendar `deleteEvent` and video `deleteMeeting` calls for `bookingRefsFiltered` before executing the subsequent reschedule email and webhook code; it must not return from the deletion block while deletions are still pending.

Every reference with a `uid` must still be handled exactly as before: `_calendar` types resolve a calendar via `getCalendar(credentialsMap.get(type))` and call `deleteEvent(uid, builder.calendarEvent, externalCalendarId)`; `_video` types call `deleteMeeting(credentialsMap.get(type), uid)`; references without `uid` (and those filtered out for missing credentials) remain skipped.
Parallel execution of the individual deletions may be preserved (e.g. `Promise.all` over `map`); a sequential `for...of` with `await` is also acceptable, provided all deletions are awaited.
References with a falsy `uid`, or calendars that resolve to `undefined` (so `deleteEvent` is not called), must not cause the flow to throw or skip other references.
items.notes: The finding's claim of a 'try/catch around forEach' is not supported by the shown code — no try/catch is visible around lines 553-567, so that part is overstated; the core defect (unawaited async callbacks) is correct. Note that awaiting via `Promise.all` changes error semantics from silently-ignored rejections to a thrown rejection that fails the mutation; a fix that instead collects settlements and continues (e.g. `Promise.allSettled`) is also a valid way to meet the 'all deletions complete before continuing' obligation, so the grader should not require literal `Promise.all`.

items.defectStatement: In getClient (lines 75-99), the service unconditionally requests a new Salesforce access token on every client construction, checks success with `response.statusText !== "OK"` (which misclassifies an empty HTTP/2 status text as an error and is not a reliable HTTP success check), and writes refreshed tokens to the DB—yet it still builds the jsforce.Connection from the original `credentialKey.access_token`. This causes an unnecessary network call and DB write on every service use and ignores the token it just refreshed.
obligations: Do not refresh unconditionally: getClient must reuse the existing stored access token when it is present and not expired (or otherwise known invalid), and only perform a refresh when required.

Use a reliable HTTP success check such as `response.ok` instead of comparing `statusText` to "OK"; an empty statusText must not be treated as an error, and the JSON should only be parsed after a successful response.

When a refresh occurs, the refreshed access token must be used for the returned jsforce.Connection (and persisted consistently with the refresh_token preserved if the response omits it), not the stale `credentialKey.access_token`.

Persist updated credentials only when a refresh actually happens, not on every getClient call; if credential sync provides external OAuth client credentials, use those rather than blindly using Cal.com's own app keys.
items.notes: The finding correctly identifies the unconditional fetch/DB write and the statusText bug. It omits that the refreshed token is persisted but then not passed to jsforce.Connection; a correct fix should address that too. `refreshOAuthTokens` is one valid implementation but is not required if the behavioral obligations are met. The credential-sync concern cannot be verified from the cited lines alone and may depend on surrounding code; treat it as contextual.

items.defectStatement: In the async legacy Create goroutine, the error from d.Legacy.Create is captured in errObjectSt but never reported: line 56 only converts it to a boolean for d.recordLegacyDuration, so a failure (or timeout) of the legacy write is silently swallowed and there is no log trace of legacy drift. The finding is accurate for lines 55-56, though it is scoped to the Create goroutine; the same pattern appears in the Update/Delete/DeleteCollection goroutines in this file.
obligations: When errObjectSt is non-nil, an error-level log entry including the error is emitted; the pre-PR behavior of logging the legacy-create failure must be restored.
When errObjectSt is nil, no error log is emitted (no spurious error entries on the happy path).
The existing metric call d.recordLegacyDuration(errObjectSt != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy) is preserved with the same arguments/semantics.
The goroutine still runs asynchronously and Create still returns (created, err) from the Storage write unchanged; the async legacy path must not block or alter the returned result.
items.notes: Any logging mechanism using the available logger is acceptable: the goroutine's ctx carries the contextual logger (klog.NewContext(ctx, log) at line 39), so either klog.FromContext(ctx).Error(...) or reusing log/closured logger works. Logging should happen before or after the metric call; order is not graded. A grader should not require an exact message string, but the entry must carry the error value (e.g. errObjectSt) and not just a boolean/derived error. Trap: replacing the boolean with errObjectSt or logging errObjectSt.Error() alone would lose structure, but is still a valid fix; do not demand a specific API. The finding mentions other goroutines (Update line ~176, Delete line ~112, DeleteCollection) — a fix touching only lines 55-56 satisfies the cited-lines scope, but a grader may note the cited range covers only the Create goroutine.

items.defectStatement: In useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable returns loading:false when rule is undefined, so `MaybeSupported = loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported` becomes AlwaysSupported for the skipToken case; consequently duplicateSupported is AlwaysSupported and AlertRuleAction.Duplicate resolves to just the Grafana rules 'create' permission, reporting Duplicate as allowed with no rule present. A second concern in the finding is overstated: this hook is for Grafana-managed rules (GrafanaPromRuleDTO), not for data-source rules, so the mechanism is 'undefined rule => AlwaysSupported', not any OR-ing onto arbitrary non-Grafana rules.
obligations: When the rule argument is undefined (e.g. skipToken), AlertRuleAction.Duplicate must resolve to not-allowed regardless of whether the user holds the Grafana rules create permission.

When a real, non-plugin-provided GrafanaPromRuleDTO is supplied and it is not loading, Duplicate must still be allowed exactly when the user has the Grafana rules create permission (existing behavior preserved).

When rule is undefined, the rule-dependent abilities (Update, Delete, Pause, Restore, DeletePermanently) must remain not-allowed, and View/Explore must keep their current permission-gated behavior; do not regress these while fixing Duplicate.

The loading-while-unresolved semantics must be preserved: while the folder/permission state is loading for a defined rule, abilities that depend on support must stay unsupported rather than assuming AlwaysSupported.
items.notes: Several valid fixes exist: add `!rule` to the MaybeSupported condition (`!rule || loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported`), have useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable report loading/not-editable for a missing rule, or special-case duplicateSupported. The grader should accept any of these as long as the obligations hold. The finding's claim that this is OR-ed into canDuplicate 'for every non-Grafana (data-source) rule' is inaccurate; only the GrafanaPromRuleDTO path (skipToken/undefined rule) is at issue here. Note also that isPluginProvidedRule(undefined) and prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(undefined) are expected to return false, so Silence/ModifyExport/Pause/... depend on other predicates and are not the primary defect.

items.defectStatement: In Run (pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77), the periodic ticker that drives the full cleanup job set was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`, so every one of the eight cleanup jobs (tmp files, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, user invites, short URLs, query history) now fires up to 10x more often, multiplying DB/IO load with no justification. The command is exactly as cited: the diff confirms 10 -> 1 on that line.
obligations: The unconditional periodic interval for the full cleanup job set must not be 1 minute; a 10-minute (600s) interval must be restored as the default cadence.

If a faster cadence is added at all, it must be gated behind configuration, must default to the previous 10-minute behavior, and must not cause the full set of DB-touching jobs to run at the faster rate.

Existing Run semantics must be preserved: the one-shot srv.cleanUpTmpFiles(ctx) call before the ticker, a select on ticker.C and ctx.Done(), returning ctx.Err() on cancellation, and clean()'s 9-minute timeout unchanged.
No other behavior or callers may change: the job list, ordering, and per-job logic in clean() stay as-is.
items.notes: Any of these fixes is acceptable: revert to time.Minute*10; or keep a 1-minute ticker but run only the annotation cleaner each tick and the remaining jobs every N-th tick; or add a config setting whose default is 10 minutes. Partially mitigating (but not exonerating) the finding: clean() runs synchronously inside the select with a 9-minute timeout and the ticker channel only buffers one tick, so a slow run drops ticks and the real increase can be under 10x — the defect direction and the need to restore the 10-minute default still hold. Grading should check that the interval / cadence gate, not just the literal token, prevents the full job set from running every minute.

items.defectStatement: In DualWriterMode3.Delete, the successful-path storage metric call at line 106 passes `name` (the deleted object's name) into the kind label position of `recordStorageDuration`, while the error path (line 103) and the legacy path (line 113) pass `options.Kind`. This mislabels the metric and creates one unbounded time series per object name.
obligations: The third argument passed to `recordStorageDuration` on the success path of Delete must be `options.Kind` (the resource kind), not `name`.
All other arguments on that call must stay unchanged: `false` (no error), `mode3Str`, `method` ("delete"), and `startStorage`.

The metric emission must remain on the success path only, i.e. still after the `err != nil` early return and before/independent of the legacy goroutine, preserving existing control flow and return values.
The label value must now match the kind used by the other metric calls in this function and file (e.g. lines 103 and 113), so the metric's label set is consistent.
items.notes: Only line 106 needs to change; a fix that also touches argument order/other args, or moves the call, is wrong. Unrelated pre-existing oddity at line 97 (`klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` instead of `log`) is outside the cited line and not part of this finding.

items.defectStatement: The filter at lines 74-78 performs case-sensitive comparisons for existing attendees and compares the already-lowercased blacklist against the raw guest email. Consequently, an existing attendee such as `Foo@Example.com` and a submitted `foo@example.com` are treated as different, and an uppercase form of a blacklisted email bypasses the blacklist filter.
obligations: A guest email that matches an existing booking attendee email case-insensitively must be excluded from `uniqueGuests`.
A guest email whose lowercase form equals an entry in `blacklistedGuestEmails` must be excluded regardless of the guest's original casing.
When a guest is accepted, its original email casing must be preserved for the created attendee record and outbound emails; normalization must be used only for comparison.
The existing all-filtered-out behavior must be preserved: if `uniqueGuests` is empty, the same `BAD_REQUEST` `emails_must_be_unique_valid` error is thrown and no booking update/email flow occurs.
items.notes: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is already lowercased at lines 70-72, so only the guest side needs normalization for that check; the attendee email side also needs normalization for the duplicate check. The cited filter also does not deduplicate `guests` against each other, but that is a pre-existing behavior outside the case-sensitivity defect stated here.

items.defectStatement: In SpanFlusher.join(), the loop over self.processes breaks as soon as the deadline (deadline - time.time()) is <= 0, so any processes not yet reached in iteration are neither polled until they exit nor passed to process.terminate(); only the process being visited when the deadline expired (or those visited earlier) is terminated. The previous single-process implementation always called terminate() after the wait, so hung/remaining worker processes now survive past join() until interpreter exit.
obligations: When a timeout is provided and the deadline elapses before all processes have been visited, terminate() must still be called on every remaining multiprocessing.Process in self.processes (none may be skipped because of the deadline).
Processes reached before the deadline must retain current behavior: wait (poll) until the process is no longer alive or the deadline passes, then call terminate() if it is a multiprocessing.Process.
join() must not block past the supplied deadline while waiting for processes (no unbounded waits after the deadline is reached).

Behavior when timeout is None must be unchanged: iterate all processes, wait for each while it is alive, and terminate each multiprocessing.Process; non-Process entries (e.g. threading.Thread when produce_to_pipe is set) must not have terminate()/kill() called on them.
items.notes: Valid fixes include not breaking (continue to the terminate step for the remaining entries), or breaking out of the wait loop and then doing a second pass that terminates all not-yet-terminated processes. A fix that terminates everything up front before waiting would violate obligation 2 (order wait-then-terminate is expected). The finding is accurate as written; only nuance is the 'leaked until interpreter exit' wording — the processes are daemon=True, so they are reaped at interpreter exit, but they still consume resources and are not managed by join(). The unused process_index in the loop header is incidental, not part of this defect.

items.defectStatement: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close and terminate both unconditionally call self.queue_pool.shutdown(). The FixedQueuePool is injected via the constructor (and per the finding is factory-shared across create_with_partitions calls), so closing one strategy tears down the pool still used by another live strategy: subsequent queue.put calls can raise queue.ShutDown, and offset tracking/commits are orphaned. In addition, terminate does not join self.commit_thread, so a stale commit loop can continue invoking an obsolete commit_function after teardown.
obligations: close and terminate must not shut down a FixedQueuePool that may still be shared with another active strategy; shutdown responsibility must move to the pool/factory owner or be reference-counted, or each strategy must own its pool.
Both close and terminate must stop and join the strategy's own commit_thread, so no stale commit_function is called after the strategy is closed.
Existing per-strategy commit behavior must be preserved: offsets are only marked committed after commit_function succeeds, and commit only occurs while the strategy is active.
Preserve graceful close semantics (draining/joining in-flight work before teardown) and immediate terminate semantics for work owned by this strategy.
items.notes: The shown code injects queue_pool rather than creating it, which makes the finding plausible; however, the exact sharing behavior depends on the factory/create_with_partitions caller, which is not in this window and should be confirmed. Valid fixes include (a) making the pool per-strategy, (b) moving pool shutdown to the factory/owner with refcounting or an explicit last-user check, or (c) having close leave the shared pool alone while terminate force-shuts it only when this strategy owns it. The missing join in terminate is a real secondary defect, but the primary regression is the shared-pool shutdown. The finding's 'puts raise ShutDown' consequence is accurate because FixedQueuePool.shutdown calls queue.shutdown(immediate=False).

items.defectStatement: BuildIndex no longer holds cacheMu across the build (the outer Lock/defer Unlock was removed), so mutual exclusion now covers only the final b.cache[key] = idx write. Two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource can therefore both reach bleve.New on the same directory (filepath.Join(Root, Namespace, Resource.Group)), run the builder and Flush in parallel, clobber each other's cache entry last-wins, and double-count IndexTenants.
obligations: Concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key must be mutually exclusive for the build portion (the bleve.New/builder/Flush section): at most one goroutine may build a given key at a time, and a caller arriving during an in-flight build must either wait for it and reuse the resulting index, or otherwise avoid issuing a second concurrent bleve.New/builder/Flush on the same directory.
The cache map write must remain protected: b.cache[key] = idx (and any read of b.cache) must still be guarded by cacheMu or an equivalent lock so the map is not accessed concurrently.
The exclusion must be per-key, not global: builds for distinct keys must remain free to proceed in parallel; do not reintroduce a single backend-wide lock held for the whole function.

On error paths (bleve.New, builder, or Flush returning an error) any added lock/once/singleflight state for that key must be released or reset so the key is not left permanently locked and a later build can retry.
items.notes: The pre-diff code held one global cacheMu for the entire function, which serialized builds for all keys (that is what the diff removed); a correct fix must not simply revert to that global lock, hence the per-key requirement. The diff's intent (allow parallel builds across different keys) is fine; only same-key exclusion was lost. Also note the cited lines alone (the cache-write lock) cannot restore build exclusion, since the build occurs earlier in the function (lines ~94-135); a fix expressed only at lines 137-140 can at best keep the map write safe, and per-key exclusion has to be arranged where the build happens. Double-counting of IndexTenants.Inc is a real but secondary consequence of the duplicate build. TotalDocs (line 146) and other b.cache readers are unlocked, a separate pre-existing race not charged to this finding.

items.defectStatement: In `_commit_loop` (lines 273-291) the strategy invokes the caller-supplied `commit_function` from a dedicated background thread that runs concurrently with the Arroyo main thread's `poll`/`submit`/`close`/`terminate`. That callback is an Arroyo commit handler that touches StreamProcessor/consumer state and is intended to be driven from the main thread, so concurrent invocation can race with `poll`/`_run_once` and can commit offsets for partitions that have just been revoked; additionally, because `shutdown_event.wait(1.0)` returns immediately once the event is set, the body still executes a final `commit_function` call after `close()`/`terminate()` has begun shutting things down.
obligations: `commit_function` must not be executed concurrently with the main thread's processing lifecycle: commits must either be performed on the main thread (e.g. from `poll`/`submit`) or serialized against the main thread by a shared lock, so a commit can never overlap an in-flight `poll`/`_run_once`/`submit`.

No commit may be issued after shutdown begins: once `close()`/`terminate()` (or `shutdown_event.set()`) has run, the background path must not call `commit_function` again, and `close()` must still join the commit thread so it cannot commit during/after `queue_pool.shutdown()`.

Offset bookkeeping semantics must be preserved: offsets are still derived from `offset_tracker.get_committable_offsets()`, only contiguous/processed offsets are committed, `mark_committed` is only applied after a successful `commit_function` call, the `offsets_committed` metric is still emitted for non-empty committable sets, and exceptions are logged rather than propagating to kill the loop/thread.

The public API and worker behavior must be unchanged: the `submit`/`poll`/`close`/`terminate`/`join` signatures and the decoding, grouping, queue submission, and offset-completion logic in `submit` and the workers continue to work as before.
items.notes: Both suggested approaches are valid: (a) have the background loop only compute committable offsets and stash them for the main thread to commit in `poll()`/`submit()`, or (b) keep committing in the thread but guard it with a lock shared with the main thread and skip/drop when closed. A grader should accept either. Real traps: the `while not shutdown_event.is_set(): ... wait()` pattern means a final commit happens after the event is set unless explicitly guarded; `terminate()` currently sets the event without joining the commit thread, so any fix must also prevent post-terminate commits. The finding is slightly overstated in that the underlying confluent Kafka consumer's `commit` is documented as thread-safe, so the primary defect is the StreamProcessor-level/revocation race and the missing shutdown guard, not raw consumer corruption; do not require an implementation that reimplements Kafka's commit.

items.defectStatement: FixedQueuePool creates each worker queue with queue.Queue() (no maxsize), so the queues are unbounded and FixedQueuePool.submit() unconditionally calls work_queue.put() with no capacity/depth check. If producers (SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit) outpace the single worker thread per queue, items accumulate without bound and can exhaust memory; the class docstring's promise of "Natural backpressure when queues fill up" is not actually implemented.
obligations: Each queue created in FixedQueuePool.__init__ must have a finite capacity (maxsize > 0, e.g. passed as a constructor argument) so queue depth cannot grow without bound.

When the target queue is at capacity, submit() must apply backpressure by waiting/blocking until space is available rather than dropping items, raising a spurious error, or silently discarding/reordering work.

Group-to-queue routing (get_queue_for_group / consistent hashing) and FIFO-per-queue ordering must be preserved, and submit() must still call offset_tracker.add_offset(partition, offset) for every item that is actually enqueued so the commit loop's contiguous-offset logic stays correct.

Existing public behavior must be preserved: submit(group_key, work_item) -> None signature and semantics, worker construction/start, get_stats()/qsize() stats, wait_until_empty(), and graceful shutdown() must continue to work (including that a blocked submit interacts sanely with queue.shutdown()).
items.notes: The finding is accurate as stated; the docstring on SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy (line 253) claiming "Natural backpressure when queues fill up" corroborates that backpressure was intended and is missing. Valid fixes include: passing maxsize to queue.Queue() and keeping put() blocking (default block=True), or an explicit depth-limit/backpressure check before enqueueing; both satisfy the obligations, so graders should accept either. Traps to watch: maxsize must be > 0 (0 or negative means infinite), do not confuse this with the Queue.shutdown() usage on the shutdown path, and a bounded queue's put() can raise queue.ShutDown after q.shutdown(), so the fix should not turn that into an unhandled exception in normal shutdown flow. The cited range includes get_queue_for_group (lines 198-202), which is not itself defective; the defect is confined to the queue construction at line 185 and the unbounded put at line 212.

items.defectStatement: In gen_request_data (lines 153-155), error timestamps originate from nodestore event data (epoch seconds, e.g. ~1.7e9) while replay/rrweb breadcrumb event 'timestamp' values are epoch milliseconds (e.g. ~1.7e12), so the comparison `error_events[error_idx]['timestamp'] < event.get('timestamp', 0)` is always true. Consequently every error is emitted before the first breadcrumb, so the chronological ordering sent to Seer is wrong (all errors clumped at the front). The finding is accurate.
obligations: The error timestamp and the replay event timestamp must be compared in the same unit (e.g. multiply the error timestamp by 1000, or divide the event timestamp by 1000) so that an error is emitted only when it actually precedes the breadcrumb.

Interleaving must be chronologically correct: an error must be emitted after every breadcrumb that precedes it and before the first breadcrumb that follows it; errors later than all breadcrumbs must still be emitted at the end, and errors earlier than the first breadcrumb must still be emitted before it.
No error may be dropped or duplicated, and the existing ascending sort of error_events must remain consistent with whatever unit normalization is applied.

Existing behavior and callers must be preserved: gen_request_data / get_request_data signatures and the segment-iteration and as_log_message filtering logic stay unchanged, and the error log message still represents the User experienced an error.
Replay events lacking a 'timestamp' key must not be broken by the normalization (the current default of 0 for the missing-key case must not inadvertently suppress or reorder errors).
items.notes: Several fixes are valid: normalize when building ErrorEvent in fetch_error_details, or normalize inside gen_request_data (and optionally in the comparison only vs. also in generate_error_log_message). Whether the timestamp printed in generate_error_log_message ends up in seconds or milliseconds is an implementation choice and should not by itself fail the fix, provided ordering is correct. The finding is not overstated; the unit mismatch is real (nodestore error event data 'timestamp' is epoch seconds, rrweb event 'timestamp' is epoch ms). Secondary/minor (not required to fix): the `event.get('timestamp', 0)` fallback of 0 would, on a missing timestamp, make the comparison always false for that event; and error_events is sorted but only used here.

items.defectStatement: The useQuery cache key for trace-item attribute keys is ['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions], and queryOptions is built only from traceItemType, type, datetime and projectIds — no organization identifier. Since the fetcher (getTraceItemAttributeKeys, which internally reaches the org-scoped /trace-items/attributes/ endpoint) does depend on the current organization, switching orgs with otherwise-identical selection inputs (e.g. the default all-projects '-1' selection with the same datetime/type) will reuse the previous org's cached TagCollection, showing cross-org attribute keys until a refetch.
obligations: The cache key (or a value included in queryOptions that is part of the key) must incorporate the current organization identifier, so that two different organizations with otherwise-identical inputs never share a cached entry.

Within the same organization, the key must still distinguish entries by datetime, projectIds, type and traceItemType, and identical inputs must still map to the same cache entry (no gratuitous cache fragmentation).
The fix must preserve the hook's existing external behavior and return contract: enabled gating, the previous-data fallback (attributes = isFetching ? previous : data), isLoading and error.
Any added organization value must be reactively sourced and reflected in the useMemo dependency list so the key updates on org change without stale closures.
items.notes: Multiple valid fixes exist: adding the org slug/id as another element of the queryKey array, or threading an org identifier into makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions/queryOptions (which is already part of the key) — the grader should accept either and not require a specific shape. Trap: verify whether the delegated useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys/makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions already embeds an org identifier; if it does, the finding is invalid, but on the shown code queryOptions contains none. Also note: if callers always pass explicit global-unique project IDs, collisions are limited to the all-projects/'-1' default selection, so the finding is slightly overstated in frequency but still correct in substance.

items.defectStatement: getClientsWithPermission derives client ids from resources of type AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE and adds resource.getName(). The realm's 'type' resource for that type (the all-clients resource) has the literal name "Clients", so that value is added to the result, and per-client resources are not covered by this lookup, so the method does not reliably return the realm's client ids that the caller (AvailableRoleMappingResource) resolves clients by.
obligations: Every element returned must be the identifier of an actual client of this realm, resolvable by the caller to a ClientModel (the same id form the rest of this class uses for per-client resources, i.e. ClientModel.getId()); the type/all-clients resource name (the literal "Clients") must never be returned.
Clients for which the requested scope is effectively granted (per-client resource grant, or an all-clients grant) must appear in the result; clients with no grant of the scope must not appear.
A client's identity must be derived per-client (resource name / client lookup), not from a name shared by all clients or by the resource type.

Preserve the existing short-circuits: an empty Set is returned when root.isAdminSameRealm() is false or root.realmResourceServer() is null, and the method signature/return type (Set<String>) is unchanged.
items.notes: The finding's premise that per-client resources have no type set in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource is outside the shown window and may be wrong; if the type is set there, findByType also returns per-client resources and the only defect is the stray "Clients" entry (the identifier form then already matches client.getId()). The finding's alternative of mapping to client.getClientId() is suspect: this class looks up per-client resources by client.getId(), so a fix must return whatever identifier AvailableRoleMappingResource resolves with. Valid fixes include: skipping resources whose name equals AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, iterating the realm's clients and testing the permission per client, or setting the CLIENTS type at creation while filtering out the type resource itself.

items.defectStatement: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua lines 62-64, whenever a segment buffer grows past 1000 spans the script calls zpopmin(set_key, span_count - 1000), which removes the members with the lowest end_timestamp_precise score and applies no exemption for the segment/root span. Because scores are end_timestamp_precise, a segment span whose timestamp precedes its children's (e.g. an is_remote segment span or clock skew) can be selected as an eviction victim, so the segment later shipped by done_flush_segments can be missing its root/segment span.
obligations: When span_count > 1000, the eviction must not remove the member corresponding to the segment/root span (the payload whose span_id == set_span_id); that span must remain in set_key.

The trim must still remove the surplus spans (targeting the lowest end_timestamp_precise scores as before) so the sorted set stays bounded at ~1000 after the operation; it must not simply skip the root and leave the set permanently over the cap.
Behavior for span_count <= 1000 must be unchanged: no members are evicted.
All other behavior must be preserved: the set_key TTL/expire, the has_root_span get/setex logic, and the returned {redirect_depth, span_key, set_key, has_root_span}.
items.notes: Root spans normally have the largest end_timestamp_precise, so in the common case zpopmin already evicts them last and this only bites in the corner cases the finding names; still a real defect. Valid fixes can differ (e.g. pop victims and re-ZADD the segment span, or ZRANGEBYSCORE the candidate victims, drop all but the segment span, and ZADD it back) - grading should not require one specific implementation. TRAP: set members are serialized span payloads, not span_ids, so the segment span cannot be located by a simple ZREM by span_id; the fix must match span_id inside the payload (or otherwise track it). The rest of the file window is unchanged by the fix.

items.defectStatement: The redirect-chase loop bound was lowered from 10000 to 1000, so for a segment tree whose redirect chain is longer than ~1001 hops the loop exhausts without reaching a terminal node: `set_span_id` is left at an intermediate span, and the code then `hset`s `span_id -> <intermediate>`, merging the span into the wrong set and silently splitting/corrupting segments. The change has no functional need; the unrelated 1000-span eviction cap (`zpopmin`) added in the same diff does not require a traversal depth of 1000.
obligations: Redirect traversal must follow chains at least as deep as the prior implementation allowed (bound of 10000, i.e. 10001 iterations), so deep trees still resolve to their terminal set span.
The early-exit condition must be preserved: break when the redirect key is absent or maps a span to itself, and still return a correct `redirect_depth`.
The span-join logic and accounting must be preserved: zunionstore of span_key/parent_key into set_key, unlink of merged keys, expire, and span_count/has_root_span values returned.
The 1000-span eviction cap (`zpopmin` when span_count > 1000) must remain independent of the traversal-depth limit.
items.notes: Alternative valid fixes: restore the earlier 10000 bound, or otherwise ensure traversal is not capped at the eviction size (e.g. a separate, larger/uncapped depth constant). Traps: `for i = 0, N` performs N+1 iterations, so '10000' means 10001 hops; a fix that makes traversal unbounded/depth-aware also satisfies the requirement. The rest of the diff (set->zset, span_count, zpopmin cap, has_root_span) is out of scope for this finding and should not be reverted as part of it.

items.defectStatement: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua lines 47 and 53, `ZUNIONSTORE` is invoked without an `AGGREGATE` clause, so Redis defaults to `SUM`; when the same buffer member (same span id) is present in both the destination sorted set and the source sorted set (e.g. a redelivered/duplicated span that was already merged into its parent's set), its score is added to itself and becomes ~2x its end timestamp, so it no longer sorts by end time and is never picked up by the oldest-first `zpopmin` eviction.
obligations: Both `zunionstore` calls (the span_key merge at line 47 and the parent_key merge at line 53) must resolve members present in both input sets to a single score equal to the member's original end-timestamp score, i.e. no score addition (use `AGGREGATE MAX` or `AGGREGATE MIN`).

All members from both input sets must still be present in the destination set after the merge, with members appearing in only one set retaining their own score unchanged; cardinality (the value assigned to span_count, used for the >1000 zpopmin eviction) must remain correct.

The surrounding behavior must be unchanged: span_key/parent_key are still unlinked after a successful merge, the conditional guards (`not is_root_span`, `zcard > 0`, `set_span_id ~= parent_span_id`) stay as-is, and the expire/zpopmin logic at lines 56-64 is untouched.
items.notes: Only the two ZUNIONSTORE argument lists need editing; adding `"AGGREGATE", "MAX"` (or `"MIN"`) after the key list is the standard fix. MIN is also acceptable since duplicates carry the same timestamp; the key point is that neither SUM nor a purely zset-level workaround is valid. The finding's 'roughly doubles' is exact when the two copies share the same end timestamp. Note the guard `set_span_id ~= parent_span_id` already prevents a literal self-union (set_key == parent_key) in the second block, so the defect is specifically about duplicate members across distinct keys (redelivery after a prior merge), not about double-counting the same key twice. If the grader sees code that avoids duplicates by some other means while keeping SUM, it would still be wrong if a redelivered span can re-enter via span_key.

items.defectStatement: Making `.contents` a flex container (header.scss lines 17-18) makes the header-extra-info/title element a flex item with the default `min-width: auto`, whose automatic minimum is its min-content width; the truncating `overflow: hidden` lives on the inner `.extra-info-wrapper`, and a descendant's overflow does not zero out the item's automatic minimum. So a long, non-wrapping topic title can no longer shrink, and the `.panel` (nav) is pushed outside the header / the header overflows.
obligations: With a long, non-wrapping topic title, the header must not overflow horizontally and the `.panel` must remain inside `.contents` (right-aligned); the title must still truncate/ellipsize rather than wrap or expand the header.

The shrink constraint must land on the element that is the direct flex item of `.contents` (the header-extra-info / `.title` element), not only on a descendant such as `.extra-info-wrapper`; e.g. `min-width: 0`/`overflow: hidden`/equivalent on that item, or relocating the wrapper class onto it.
The flex-item's own overflow/ellipsis behavior for the topic title (truncation with `overflow: hidden`) must be preserved, not replaced by wrapping.
Existing header behavior must be preserved for the other children and cases: vertical centering, `.panel` pushed to the end (

Existing header behavior must be preserved for the other children and cases: vertical centering, `.panel` pushed to the end (order(3) + margin-left:auto), and the layout with no title or a short title unchanged.
items.notes: The file window/diff does not include the component markup; the deleted `.title { float: left; }` rule suggests the flex item is the element carrying `.title` (the header-extra-info component), with `.extra-info-wrapper` nested inside it — so `min-width: 0` on `.title` (or a re-added `.title` rule) is the likely fix, but any fix that constrains the true flex item is valid. Because the cited lines are only the `flexbox()`/`align-items(center)` mixins, accept fixes that leave those lines intact and add a rule elsewhere in `.d-header` scope. Do not require removing the flex container changes.

items.defectStatement: In TopicEmbed.import_remote (app/models/topic_embed.rb:48), the remote article body is fetched with `open(url)`, where `url` is derived from the user-supplied embed URL. `open`/open-uri performs a server-side HTTP request with no scheme, port, or resolved-IP restriction and follows HTTP redirects, so an embed URL pointing at an internal service (e.g. `http://host:6379/...`, `http://169.254.169.254/...`, or a redirect from an allowed host to an internal address) makes the server fetch arbitrary internal resources (SSRF).
obligations: The outbound fetch must be limited to http/https URLs; a URL with any other scheme must not be fetched.

The fetch must not be able to reach loopback/private/link-local/internal addresses (whether given directly in the URL or reached via an HTTP redirect); i.e. redirects must be disabled or each hop re-validated, and the connection host/port must not resolve to an internal address.

Normal behavior for a legitimate public embeddable URL must be preserved: `import_remote(user, url, opts)` still fetches the page, builds Readability::Document with the same tags/attributes, and returns the result of `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, opts[:title] || doc.title, doc.content)`.
The fetch must be bounded by a timeout so a slow/hanging response cannot block the request indefinitely, and a rejected/failed fetch must not raise an unhandled error into the caller path.
items.notes: The upstream `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` check referenced in the finding is not visible in this file/window, so a grader should treat it as unverified context, not as a fix in the cited lines; the cited defect is the unguarded `open(url)` call itself. Valid fixes include: replacing `open(url)` with a hardened client (e.g. open-uri with redirect disabled plus host/IP validation, or an HTTP library that supports timeouts and manual redirect handling), or pre-validating/ resolving the host and rejecting non-public addresses before reading. A fix that only checks the URL scheme is insufficient (port and IP/redirect checks are also required). Also note `open(url)` here relies on Kernel#open + open-uri; any replacement must still yield the page body string that `Readability::Document.new` consumes.

items.defectStatement: In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153, the conditional-include hook is named `include_website_name` without the trailing `?` that ActiveModel::Serializers requires for include hooks (compare `include_card_image_badge?` at line 161). AMS therefore never invokes it, so `website_name` is serialized whenever it is non-nil regardless of the viewer, and — because `:website_name` is not in the `untrusted_attributes` list at lines 105-111 that hides `:website` — viewers for whom `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true (e.g. anonymous visitors looking at restricted users) still receive the website's host/path through `website_name`. The `website.present?` guard in the method is dead code, not merely mis-conditional.
obligations: `website_name` must be omitted from the serialized payload when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true, matching how `:website` is suppressed for the same viewer.
`website_name` must still be emitted (unchanged value/format) for viewers who are allowed to see the user's unrestricted fields when the user has a website.
`website_name` must not be emitted when the user has no website (or when it resolves to nil), as the existing `website.present?` guard intends.
No other serialized attributes or unrelated serializer behavior may change.
items.notes: Two valid fix shapes exist: (a) rename the hook to `include_website_name?` and AND-in `!scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`; (b) leave the method alone and add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (the `include_*?` hook alone, or the untrusted list alone, is sufficient to satisfy obligation 1; either mechanism, or both, is acceptable — do not require a specific one). Trap: the FileDiff adds `:website_name` to an attribute list near line 40 whose identity is ambiguous from the hunk header; the FileWindow's `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111) does NOT contain `:website_name`, so the leak is real in the shown code — but a grader should confirm the current list contents before treating the finding's "not covered by untrusted_attributes" claim as still true. Also note the leak is only partial: `website_name` returns a host/path, not the full raw URL, so it is a redaction gap rather than raw `website` exposure.

items.defectStatement: The defect is not in the shown line itself — `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` in `ApplicationController#set_locale` is correct. The problem is incompleteness: fallback locales are loaded only on the web-request path, while other entry points that set `I18n.locale` and rely on fallbacks (e.g. `PostAlerter`'s `I18n.with_locale(user.effective_locale)`, `Jobs::Base`'s locale assignment, mailers) never call `ensure_loaded!`, so fallback chains can resolve to locales that were never loaded and return missing translations.
obligations: Every code path that activates locale-dependent fallbacks (not only controller `set_locale`) must have fallback locales loaded before translations are resolved.
The web-request behavior added at line 159 must be preserved: `set_locale` still sets `I18n.locale` and ensures fallback locales are loaded without error when fallbacks are enabled.
Existing behavior when fallback locales are disabled (SiteSetting/fallback config off) must not be broken — no crash, no forced loading of unwanted locales.
Loading must remain safe/idempotent for repeated calls (per-job, per-request, or per-locale-context), not re-parsing fallback data on every translation or leaking state across threads.
items.notes: The cited line is correct as written; a grader should treat the finding as 'fallback loading is under-wired' rather than 'line 159 is wrong'. Valid fixes are open-ended: centralize/hook loading into the locale-setting helper or I18n initialization, or make fallback-locale loading lazy-safe so any `I18n.locale=`/`with_locale` path triggers it. The fix likely lives outside the cited lines (PostAlerter, Jobs::Base, initializers), so do not require edits to line 159 itself beyond preserving it.

items.defectStatement: At line 35, `i.content` is dereferenced with `.scrub` before any nil check. SimpleRSS populates an item's `content` only from `content:encoded` (RSS) or Atom `<content>`; a plain RSS 2.0 item that carries only `<description>` leaves `i.content` nil, so `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError, aborting the whole import loop (and the synchronous call from TopicRetriever) instead of importing the remaining items.
obligations: An item whose `content` is nil (e.g. RSS 2.0 with only `description`) must not raise NoMethodError; a body must be obtained from `i.description` in that case.
An item that has neither content nor description must be skipped (`next`) rather than crashed on or imported with a nil/empty body.
Items that do supply `content` must still be passed to `TopicEmbed.import` with the same value as before: HTML-unescaped via CGI.unescapeHTML after scrub.
The HTML scrubbing must be applied to whichever body is used (content or description), i.e. the fallback must not bypass scrub.
items.notes: The finding is accurate as stated: SimpleRSS items return nil for absent tags, and `String#scrub` on nil raises. A minimal alternative fix (`i.content.to_s.scrub`) avoids the crash but would still import items with blank bodies, so it only partially satisfies the stated intent; a grader should treat `description` fallback plus skip-blank as the requirement. Remember `i.description` can itself be nil, so the blank check must cover both. `blank?` is available since ActiveSupport is loaded; `CGI` is available through the existing `require 'open-uri'`/Rails environment. The `url` selection on lines 32-33 is unaffected and should be preserved.

items.defectStatement: Both lookups at lines 9-11 and 15 dereference `execute(...)[0]` directly; when the query returns no rows, `[0]` is nil and `nil['id']` / `nil['value']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration. This occurs if the `embed_category` setting (or, in the fallback path, `uncategorized_category_id`) is absent.
obligations: The migration must not raise NoMethodError / IndexError when the `embed_category` query returns zero rows, nor when the `uncategorized_category_id` query returns zero rows.
When `embed_category` exists and matches a category, the resolved category_id must be that category's id (existing behavior preserved).
When `embed_category` is absent but `uncategorized_category_id` exists, the fallback must still yield that setting's value as the category_id (existing behavior preserved).

When neither lookup yields a row, `category_id` must be assigned a defined, safe default (e.g. 0/nil) so lines 25's INSERT (which requires a non-null category_id) and the rest of the migration can proceed without error.
items.notes: A guard consistent with line 19's existing pattern (`result && result.cmd_tuples > 0`) or `result.first`-style checks are both valid fixes; any approach that avoids dereferencing an empty result is acceptable. Note the second query's setting `uncategorized_category_id` is a core Discourse setting and usually present, so the line-11 crash is the more likely real failure, but both dereferences are genuinely unguarded. The finding is accurate; not overstated.

items.defectStatement: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90) the membership row is deleted via `group.users.delete(user_id)`, but nothing clears the removed user's `primary_group_id` when it points at this group. Such a user keeps the group as their primary group, so its flair/title continue to be applied even though they are no longer a member. The cited line confirms the missing reset.
obligations: After a removal, if the removed user's `primary_group_id` equals this group's id, that value must be persisted as nil (so the group's flair/title no longer applies).

The membership deletion itself must still occur for the targeted user, and the endpoint's existing contract must be preserved: `can_not_modify_automatic` guard for automatic groups, `success_json` on success, `render_json_error` on failure.
Users other than the removed one, and the removed user when their `primary_group_id` is some other group (or already nil), must not be modified.
Removal must remain safe when `user_id` does not correspond to an existing user (no exception) and must stay correct if the same removal is repeated (idempotent no-op on the primary-group reset).
items.notes: Any implementation is acceptable: a `User.where(id: user_id, primary_group_id: group.id).update_all(primary_group_id: nil)`-style bulk update, a model helper that already clears the primary group (e.g. Group#remove with the user object, if that method performs the reset), or a direct `user.update(primary_group_id: nil)`; the reset must be persisted, not just set in memory. The finding's claim that the old `destroy_deletions`/`remove` path did this reset is not verifiable from the shown window, but the behavioral defect is real regardless. Note the finding says the primary group affects 'flair and title' — correct; do not over-specify that the reset must happen before or after `group.users.delete`.

items.defectStatement: In TopicsController#unsubscribe, `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` (line 105) can return nil for a user who has no TopicUser row for the topic (e.g. someone who received a notification/email without ever opening the topic). Line 107 then calls `tu.notification_level`, so a nil `tu` raises NoMethodError and the unsubscribe link 500s.
obligations: When no TopicUser row exists for the current user and topic, `unsubscribe` must not raise NoMethodError (no method call on a nil `tu`) and must complete the request successfully (still reaching perform_show_response / a normal redirect-or-render path).

When a TopicUser row does exist, the existing behavior must be preserved exactly: if `tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]` set it to `regular`, otherwise set it to `muted`, and persist with `save!`.

The nil case must not be conflated with the existing-record case: the guard/short-circuit must apply only when the lookup returns nil, and must not prevent or alter the update when a record is present.

If the fix chooses to treat a missing record as needing a persisted notification level, the resulting record's notification_level must be a defined integer (not nil) so that any comparison/assignment on it cannot itself raise.
items.notes: Both a nil guard that skips the update (`if tu` / `.try`) and creating/initializing a TopicUser so the update persists are valid fixes; the finding's 'use TopicUser.get or create a record' is only one option and should not be treated as the sole accepted answer. Trap: `TopicUser.get`/`TopicUser.new` returns an unsaved record whose notification_level may be nil, so it still raises unless the level is defaulted/set; a bare `.try` guard is the minimal upstream-style fix. Also note the raised error is NoMethodError from line 107, not from `save!`. Other behavior in the action (slug redirect at line 101-103, perform_show_response at line 115) must remain unchanged.

items.defectStatement: The downsizing loop measures and re-measures the file via the open Tempfile object (`tempfile.size`), and `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` may replace the path with a new inode while the Tempfile's descriptor still points at the original large file. As a result the loop re-evaluates a stale size (spinning all 5 attempts without converging) and `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile, filename, tempfile.size, ...)` reads the original, non-downsized content/size, so the automatic reduction effectively does not take effect.
obligations: The size used to terminate the loop and the size passed to Upload.create_for must reflect the file as it exists on disk after downsizing (e.g. File.size(tempfile.path) or a re-opened Tempfile), not a cached/fstat size of the original inode.
The data handed to Upload.create_for must be the downsampled bytes, even when ImageMagick produces the result by writing a new file and renaming it over tempfile.path.

The existing guard/loop semantics must be preserved: only run when tempfile is present, tempfile.size > 0, max_image_size_kb > 0, and FileHelper.is_image?(filename); at most 5 downsize attempts; stop once the file is at or below max_image_size_kb.kilobytes.
The Tempfile passed to Upload.create_for must remain a usable readable IO/path for that call, and the existing `ensure tempfile.try(:close!)` cleanup must still succeed.
items.notes: Multiple fixes are valid: reopen the Tempfile (e.g. tempfile.open + rewind) or re-derive size/content from tempfile.path after downsizing; the grader should not require one specific mechanism. The finding's claim that downsizing 'effectively does nothing' is accurate only when ImageMagick lands the output in a new inode (write+rename) rather than truncating in place; a correct fix must not depend on which ImageMagick does. Do not remove the loop, the attempt cap, or the ensure block. The companion content_type assignment for the URL branch is unrelated to this finding.

items.defectStatement: In setupController (lines 8-12) model.findMembers() is invoked with no arguments, so the public group members page fetches only the server's default page (limit 50, offset 0); since group/members.hbs exposes no pagination/offset controls, members beyond the first 50 of a non-automatic group are unreachable in the view. The finding is accurate about the cited lines, but note the 50-member cap originates from the endpoint change, not from these lines (the removed afterModel also called findMembers() with no arguments) — lines 8-12 are simply where the client must now request more than the default page. Secondary point visible in the cited code: the promise returned by findMembers() is dropped (not returned or awaited), unlike the old afterModel, so nothing waits for the members to load.
obligations: The call on the cited lines must not depend on the server's default single page of 50 members: a public (non-automatic) group's full member list must be reachable from this view, either by requesting all members or by driving pagination/offset from this call.

Any limit/offset or 'load all' intent passed to findMembers() must be a value the endpoint actually honors (a valid, sufficiently large limit or a real offset), so that more than the first 50 members are returned.

Existing behavior must be preserved: this.controllerFor('group').set('showing', 'members') still runs and the controller's model is still set to the object that group/members.hbs renders (the group with its members).
Automatic groups (e.g. owner/trust-level groups) must continue to load and render as before; the change must not break their member (or empty) display.
items.notes: The regression is really server-side pagination; the cited JS was always a single no-arg call, so a fix may legitimately just request all members here. Only the cited lines are replaced, so do not make the fix depend on template/pagination-UI changes. If the fix takes an offset/limit, it should be a constant or derived value available in the route, not a UI control. The unawaited findMembers() promise is a real secondary issue in these lines but is not what the finding is about; a fix that awaits/returns it is fine but not required unless it changes rendering behavior.

items.defectStatement: In src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11-12, MetricAlertDetectorHandler was changed to subclass StatefulDetectorHandler with an empty body, so the abstract members inherited from StatefulDetectorHandler (reported as counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data) are never implemented. Since StatefulDetectorHandler uses ABCMeta, the class can no longer be instantiated, which makes `group_type.detector_handler(self)` in Detector.detector_handler (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:86) raise TypeError for any Detector whose type resolves to MetricAlertFire; the previous version was concrete (it defined evaluate), so this is a regression.
obligations: MetricAlertDetectorHandler must be instantiable: constructing it (equivalently, evaluating Detector.detector_handler for a MetricAlertFire-typed Detector) must not raise a TypeError about remaining abstract methods.

No abstract members inherited from StatefulDetectorHandler may remain unimplemented on MetricAlertDetectorHandler (either implement/override them with concrete bodies, or derive from a concrete base that supplies them).

The handler must honor StatefulDetectorHandler's contract for the methods it provides so it can be used safely; because MetricAlertFire issues are not yet created, no-op/stub implementations that return correctly-typed values (as the prior `evaluate` returning [] did) are acceptable.
Existing wiring must be preserved: MetricAlertFire.detector_handler still points at MetricAlertDetectorHandler, the module still imports successfully, and the GroupType fields/behavior are unchanged.
items.notes: The list of specific abstract method names comes from the finding and should be confirmed against the actual StatefulDetectorHandler definition before grading. Valid fixes include implementing the four hooks as stubs, implementing the required methods with real logic, or making the class a concrete subclass/alias of a concrete handler; a fix that only overrides evaluate() clears the abstract state solely if evaluate is the (only) abstract member. Note the pre-change code was itself a no-op stub (returned []), so the regression is the un-instantiability, not lost alerting behavior.

items.defectStatement: When the 'use-table-widget-visualization' feature flag is enabled, tableResultComponent renders TableWidgetVisualization with hard-coded empty columns={[]} and empty tableData data/meta, ignoring the real result.data, result.meta, and widget.queries[i] fields; every table widget therefore renders with no data.
obligations: In the feature-flag branch, TableWidgetVisualization must receive the current iteration's real table data and metadata, not empty placeholders: tableData.data must reflect result.data and tableData.meta must convey result.meta (including its fields/units) so rows render.
columns must be populated from the relevant widget query/result metadata (for example, from widget.queries[i].fields/stripped fields or result.meta.fields) instead of remaining an empty array.

The existing non-flag StyledSimpleTableChart branch must remain behaviorally unchanged, including fields/fieldAliases/title/loading handling/metadata/data/stickyHeaders/fieldHeaderMap/custom renderer/minColumnWidth.
The per-result mapping must be preserved: each tableResults entry should get its own data/metadata/columns, and existing guard behavior for undefined tableResults should not regress.
items.notes: Any valid derivation of columns is acceptable as long as real columns and data are supplied; a fix may source columns from result.meta.fields or widget.queries[i].fields as the SimpleTableChart path does. The finding is accurate as written. A common trap is passing only result.data while leaving TableWidgetVisualization's expected meta.fields/meta.units empty or malformed; graders should check that actual metadata is propagated, not just that the arrays are non-empty.

items.defectStatement: In `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` (lines 55-63), the check `column_lower == "count()"` only matches the exact, unaliased string `count()`; any valid equivalent y-axis expression such as `count() as total`, `count( )`, or other canonical/spacing variants falls through to the `else` branch and is passed through unchanged. As a result those queries keep returning unweighted `count()` values for allowlisted (upsampled) projects, silently breaking the upsampling contract.
obligations: Any y-axis expression that denotes a bare count aggregate, regardless of case, internal whitespace inside the parentheses, or an attached alias, must be converted to the upsampled form; expressions that are not bare `count()` (e.g. `count_unique()`, `count_if(...)`, `epm()`, plain field names) must be left unchanged.

Aliasing must be preserved: if the input was `count() as total`, the output must still carry the same alias (e.g. `upsampled_count() as total`); the hardcoded alias `count` may only be supplied when the input had no alias.
Column order, count, and non-transformed column strings must be preserved exactly (output list length equals input length, untouched columns returned verbatim).
The emitted expression must be syntactically valid for the downstream search/query parser used by the endpoint (function name plus optional alias).
items.notes: The finding is accurate: the cited comparison is an exact string equality and does miss aliased/spaced forms. Some input normalization may already have happened upstream, but the function itself does not guarantee canonical form, so the requirement stands. Multiple valid fixes exist (regex on the raw string, or parsing via sentry.search.events parser and checking the parsed function name); a grader should accept any approach meeting the obligations. Trap: a fix that transforms aliased counts but rewrites the alias to `count` (dropping the user's alias) violates obligation 2. Also ensure case-insensitivity is retained, since the current code lowercases before matching.

items.defectStatement: In OrderedQueueWorker.run, the finally block at lines 148-149 unconditionally calls self.offset_tracker.complete_offset(...), so a work item whose result_processor raised (non-ShutDown exception) is marked complete and its offset becomes committable, causing the commit loop to advance past a message that was never successfully processed. The strategy docstring promises 'Only commits offsets after successful processing', so this silently drops failed messages.
obligations: On the success path, when result_processor returns normally, complete_offset(work_item.partition, work_item.offset) must still be called so the item's offset can be committed.
On a non-queue.ShutDown exception from result_processor, complete_offset must NOT be called for that work item; its offset must remain outstanding so get_committable_offsets cannot advance past it.
The existing failure logging (logger.exception('Unexpected error in queue worker', extra={'worker_id': self.worker_id})) must be preserved.
The queue-depth metrics.gauge emission must still run after each dequeued item, and the worker must keep looping (process subsequent items) rather than propagating the exception out of run.
items.notes: Finding is accurate as written. Any structure is acceptable as long as failure does not complete the offset: a success flag set inside the try and checked in finally, or moving complete_offset out of finally into the try after result_processor, or an else clause on the try. Note the pre-existing `except queue.ShutDown: break` path also falls through finally and currently completes the offset; a success-flag fix will also skip complete_offset on that path. Treat that as acceptable (the item was not processed), but do not fail a fix solely for it — the graded requirement is the exception path. Do not require removing metrics.gauge from finally; only the complete_offset call must become conditional.

items.defectStatement: LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() (server-spi/.../IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:252-256) was changed to additionally require that an organization-linked IDP have its BROKER_PUBLIC config set to "true".
