Because this shared SPI predicate is not login-cache-specific — it is also used by IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate() to filter the aliases of the user's already-linked federated identities — organization-linked IDPs that are not broker-public are now silently dropped from the linked/federated IDP list shown at login and account linking, a regression for callers unrelated to the login-cache invalidation this clause was added for. Note the clause also treats a missing BROKER_PUBLIC key as false (Boolean.parseBoolean(null) == false), so any org-linked provider without that config entry is filtered out as well.
obligations: getLoginPredicate() must no longer include the `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))` clause; it must again be exactly the non-null check ANDed with the LoginFilter enum filters (ENABLED, LINK_ONLY, HIDE_ON_LOGIN), so shared consumers such as IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate() see organization-linked providers regardless of BROKER_PUBLIC.

Behavior for providers not linked to an organization must be unchanged, and the method must remain a null-safe Predicate<IdentityProviderModel> usable in the existing stream-filter call sites (same signature/return type, no new required arguments at those call sites).

If the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC login-availability condition is still needed by the login-cache invalidation code that motivated it, that condition must be preserved in a purpose-specific place (e.g. a separate dedicated predicate/method on this SPI, or applied at the invalidation call site) rather than dropped entirely — i.e. the fix must not silently reintroduce the invalidation defect it was meant to solve.
The existing getLoginSearchOptions()/LoginFilter map of search options must keep its current contents and semantics (only the predicate is in scope).
items.notes: Replacement code is scoped to lines 252-256, so the expected minimal fix is removing the added `.and(...)` line; that alone satisfies obligations 1-2 but leaves obligation 3 for the invalidation caller, which may be addressed in the same change via a new dedicated predicate or elsewhere. Alternative valid fixes: (a) drop the clause here and apply the org-public check inside the Infinispan/login-cache invalidation path, or (b) keep the clause but have IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate() use the plain enabled/linkOnly/hideOnLogin predicate — a grader should accept either as long as the shared predicate's behavior for the federated/linked-IDP caller is restored and the invalidation logic is not lost. The finding's causal claim about IdentityProviderBean.java:226 is based on the caller described in the finding, not on code visible in this file window; do not reject the fix solely on that basis. Also beware a fix that merely reorders or inverts the clause (e.g. treating null config as true) — that still leaves the org-related condition in the shared predicate and does not fix the reported regression.

items.defectStatement: get_committable_offsets iterates over every integer offset from start to max_offset and breaks at the first offset not present in all_offsets (lines 89-93). Because Kafka partition offsets are not guaranteed to be numerically contiguous, a single missing offset (e.g., 5 when offsets 4 and 6 were delivered) stops the loop, so completed offsets after the gap can never be committed and consumer lag grows without bound.
obligations: The fix must not require numerically contiguous offsets: a completed offset after a numeric gap must still be committable, provided all delivered offsets numerically before it are also completed.

The fix must not commit an offset if any delivered offset with a smaller numeric value is still outstanding; it must preserve the ordering safety guarantee that all earlier delivered work is complete.
The fix must keep commit offsets monotonic per partition and never return an offset <= last_committed[partition], while preserving the existing per-partition locking and thread-safety behavior.

The fix must preserve existing behavior for contiguous offsets and for empty/no-outstanding cases, continuing to return a dict[Partition, int] containing only partitions whose highest safe offset has advanced.
items.notes: The finding is accurate. The suggested deque-based fix is valid, but a simpler valid alternative is to compute the smallest outstanding offset and commit the largest delivered offset less than it (or max delivered if no outstanding). The grader should accept any approach that meets the obligations. The finding's 'never commits again' applies when the gap is interior to the delivered offsets; if the gap is after all delivered offsets, no problem occurs. The `offset in all_offsets` check on line 90 is redundant with `offset not in outstanding`, though the numeric contiguity assumption is the root cause.

items.defectStatement: The assertion at these lines is wrong and timing-dependent. It waits only ~0.2s after the queue drains, then asserts that test_partition was never committed (`len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`). In reality the OrderedQueueWorker marks each message's offset complete in its `finally` (including the one whose processor raised), so offsets 100 and 101 both become committable and the ~1s commit loop commits offset 102 on its next tick. The test only passes because it samples before that tick fires, i.e. it asserts the opposite of the actual commit behavior.
obligations: The test must wait deterministically for the commit to be recorded (poll `committed_offsets` in the bounded loop until test_partition appears) instead of relying on a fixed sub-second sleep; pass/fail must not depend on when the once-per-second commit tick happens.

The final assertion must assert that test_partition WAS committed with offset 102 (the next-to-read offset after processing submitted offsets 100 and 101), reflecting that the processing failure does not prevent the commit from advancing.
The test must continue to assert exactly 2 processor calls (each submitted message processed once) and keep the wait loop bounded so a genuine no-commit regression fails rather than hanging.
Offset semantics must be preserved: the committed value is last-processed-offset + 1 (compare the sibling test asserting 105 for offsets 100-104), so the expected value is 102, not 101.
items.notes: The provided window does not include OrderedQueueWorker source, so the `finally`-marks-complete mechanism cannot be re-verified here, but the cited assertion is consistent with the finding (it passes vacuously via the `or`, within 0.2s). A fix that instead changes production code so failed messages block the commit would also make a coherent test, but the finding explicitly targets the test and expects committed offset 102; grade the cited lines against that. Trap: committed-offset semantics here are next-to-read (offset+1), and the current test's docstring ('errors ... don't block offset commits for other messages') contradicts the existing assertion and may legitimately be updated.

items.defectStatement: In getSubGroups (services/.../GroupResource.java lines 176-180), the previous `canViewGlobal` short-circuit was dropped: the stream now calls `auth.groups()::canView` for every subgroup, so a caller who can view all groups (e.g. global view role / all-groups grantee) incurs one full permission evaluation per subgroup instead of a single `auth.groups().canView()` check for the whole page. This is a hot-path fanout on group listing; it does not change the filtered result set, only the cost.
obligations: The global-view fast path must be restored: check `auth.groups().canView()` at most once per request, and when it is true, skip the per-subgroup `canView(g)` evaluation entirely (e.g. a short-circuiting predicate).
For callers who are not global viewers, the result must remain the same as before: each subgroup is still filtered by `auth.groups().canView(g)`, so subgroups the caller cannot view are excluded.

The existing structure must be preserved: `auth.groups().requireView(group)` remains the first statement, and the returned stream still applies `paginatedStream(..., first, max)` and then the `.map(...)` that wraps each group with `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` / `GroupUtils.toRepresentation(auth.groups(), g, !briefRepresentation)`.
The search/exact parameters and the -1/-1 bounds on `group.getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, -1, -1)` must be unchanged.
items.notes: The finding is accurate: the diff removed `boolean canViewGlobal = auth.groups().canView();` and the `g -> canViewGlobal || auth.groups().canView(g)` predicate. This is purely a performance regression — behavior/output is equivalent, so a grader should not expect any change in returned results, only in evaluation count. Any fix that hoists a single global check and short-circuits per-group evaluation is valid; capturing the boolean in a local and using `g -> canViewGlobal || auth.groups().canView(g)` is the canonical form. Note `canView()` is an instance-method call on the same `auth.groups()` object; ensure it is invoked once, not once per stream element.

items.defectStatement: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String) (lines 215-221), when no client-specific Resource exists, the fallback assigns AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) to 'resource' and immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource). getResourceTypeResource can return null when the Clients resource-type resource is absent, so findByResource is invoked with a null resource and throws an NPE instead of the method returning false as its sibling hasPermission(String) does.
obligations: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) must return false (not throw) when the client-specific resource lookup misses and the subsequent Clients resource-type lookup (getResourceTypeResource) returns null.

Existing positive behavior must be preserved: when a client-specific resource exists, or the all-clients resource type exists and has policies, evaluation proceeds via evaluatePermission exactly as before.
The null guard must also prevent the later dereference resource.getScopes() at line 224 from being reached with a null resource.
The sibling overload hasPermission(String) (lines 237-260) must remain unchanged in behavior (returns false when its resource lookup is null).
items.notes: Valid alternatives: null-check the result of getResourceTypeResource right after the assignment (return false if null), or refactor to use the same resourceStore.findByName(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, server.getId()) lookup used by the sibling overload with a null check. Both satisfy the obligations. The finding is accurate as written; the cited lines are the correct location. Note the guard must be inside the 'resource == null' block (the outer client-specific miss), not replace the existing client-resource null check.

items.defectStatement: In GrafanaRuleListItem, the actions element is constructed with only `promRule={rule}` (the Prometheus/Grafana DTO) and never supplies ruler-rule data. RuleActionsButtons/AlertRuleMenu gates the Pause/Resume menu item on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`, so for Grafana-managed rules in the new rule list the Pause/Resume control is never rendered even when the backend reports pause is allowed.
obligations: Grafana-managed rules rendered by GrafanaRuleListItem must still expose the Pause/Resume action when the rule is pausable (not provisioned / permitted); the pause menu item must render for these rules.
The actions component must be given (or be able to obtain) the ruler-rule data/identity required to issue the pause/resume request for the rule, rather than only the Prometheus rule DTO.

Existing behavior must be preserved: provisioned (provenance) rules remain non-pausable, recording and unknown rule branches are unaffected, and other callers of RuleActionsButtons for non-Grafana rules keep working.
If ruler data is fetched on demand, the component must tolerate pending/failed fetches (no crash, no bogus pause control) instead of assuming the data is immediately present.
items.notes: The finding is accurate for the shown call site, but the grader should accept any valid mechanism: extend RuleActionsButtons/AlertRuleMenu to accept the Grafana prom rule and resolve the ruler rule internally, pass a separate ruler-rule prop, or lazily load the ruler rule. Do not require a specific prop name or shape. AlertRuleMenu and RuleActionsButtons.V2 are not in the file window, so their exact gating logic could not be independently verified here; the finding's claim about `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` is taken as given.

items.defectStatement: In DualWriterMode3.Delete (pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, lines 99-105), any error from d.Storage.Delete — including apierrors.IsNotFound — causes an immediate `return res, async, err`, so the legacy delete is never attempted. Before this change the code skipped the early return for IsNotFound and still invoked d.Legacy.Delete, so objects that exist only in legacy storage (where Storage returns NotFound) are now never cleaned up, leaving orphan legacy copies and violating the safe-measure invariant.
obligations: When d.Storage.Delete returns an error for which apierrors.IsNotFound(err) is true, Delete must NOT return early; it must still attempt to delete the object from d.Legacy.
When d.Storage.Delete returns any non-NotFound error, Delete must return that error to the caller and must not attempt a legacy delete (preserve the pre-change failure behavior).
On the success path (Storage.Delete returns nil error) the legacy delete must still be attempted as before, and the returned values (res, async, err) for the successful case must be unchanged.
A NotFound error from the legacy delete must be tolerated (logged/metrics only, not treated as a fatal condition), matching the prior handling of errLS.
items.notes: The current code performs the legacy delete inside a goroutine (lines 108-114) and never propagates its error; a valid fix can either keep that goroutine (letting the IsNotFound path fall through into it) or restructure the flow — grading should accept any shape that satisfies the obligations. The cited line numbers correspond to the Storage.Delete call and its early-return block. Unrelated defect observed but out of scope: line 106 calls recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage), passing `name` where a kind is expected.

items.defectStatement: ClientPermissionsV2.canView() (lines 85-88) only returns true for the default admin-role path (canViewClientDefault()) or the fine-grained VIEW permission on clients, while canManage() (line 73) additionally returns true for the fine-grained MANAGE permission on the all-clients resource. A caller granted only the clients MANAGE scope therefore has canManage()==true but canView()/canView(ClientModel)/canList()==false, which is inconsistent with canManage() here, with canView(ClientScopeModel) (VIEW||MANAGE, line 121), and with the V1 behavior where manage implies view.
obligations: canView() must return true when the caller holds the fine-grained clients MANAGE permission (i.e. hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), in addition to the existing conditions.
Existing true cases must be preserved: callers with the default view role path (canViewClientDefault()) or the clients VIEW permission (hasPermission(VIEW)) must still return true.

Callers holding neither VIEW nor MANAGE (and not covered by canViewClientDefault()) must still get false; no other scope (e.g. CONFIGURE, MAP_ROLES) may start granting view, and no unrelated behavior/callers should change.

The result must be consistent with canManage(): a caller granted only the all-clients MANAGE scope must have both canManage()==true and canView()==true (and consequently canView(ClientModel) via line 78).
items.notes: The finding is accurate as written; the evidence is canManage() at line 73 vs canView() at line 87. Valid fixes include adding `|| hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` to canView(), or OR-ing in a manage check, but a correct fix must remain an OR with the existing VIEW/default conditions so VIEW-only callers are unaffected (delegating to canManage() alone would wrongly drop the VIEW-only and default-role cases). Note the finding slightly overstates the role aspect: canViewClientDefault() already covers the MANAGE_CLIENTS/VIEW_CLIENTS admin roles, so the real gap is the fine-grained all-clients MANAGE permission scope. No other scope constants should be substituted.

items.defectStatement: In verifySafeHtml (lines 102-111), the common-prefix length 'start' and common-suffix length 'end' are computed independently with no overlap check, so for inputs where start + end exceeds value.length() (or sanitized.length()) the end index value.length() - end (or sanitized.length() - end) is smaller than 'start' and the substring calls throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. The finding's example is accurate: value="aaa", sanitized="aa" yields start=2, end=2, so value.substring(2, 3-2) = substring(2,1) throws, propagating out of verify() as an unhandled RuntimeException and aborting the verifier instead of adding the 'Illegal HTML in key ...' message.
obligations: For any value/sanitized pair where sanitized differs from value, including cases where the common prefix and common suffix overlap (start + end > length), the code must not throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException (or any other exception); the 'Illegal HTML in key ...' message must still be appended to messages.

All substring (or equivalent) indices must satisfy 0 <= from <= to <= length for both the value and the sanitized string; value and sanitized must be bounded independently, since their lengths differ.

For the non-overlapping cases the current behavior must be preserved: the message still shows the differing middle region with the identical prefix and suffix stripped, in the existing "'<value middle>' vs. '<sanitized middle>'" format.
The containing control flow must be preserved: the check is still inside the if (!Objects.equals(sanitized, value)) block per key, and sanitizeAnchors/normalizeValue behavior is unaffected.
items.notes: Alternative fixes are acceptable: clamp end to the remaining length (e.g. end = Math.min(end, value.length() - start) and similarly for sanitized), or clamp the substring bounds as the finding suggests (Math.min/Math.max), or recompute the suffix after accounting for the prefix. The finding's suggested clamp is valid only in that it avoids the exception; a grader should accept any fix producing in-bounds indices and a sensible differing-region message. The bug is reachable whenever the sanitizer shortens a string that begins and ends with the same character run (the lengths differ by definition since sanitized != value, but the crash requires genuine overlap). Only IOException is caught in verify(), so this RuntimeException aborts the whole build. The finding is not overstated: the loop bounds cap start and end individually at the shorter length but never constrain their sum.

items.defectStatement: In bleveBackend.TotalDocs (pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:144-154) the loop `for _, v := range b.cache` reads the map without holding b.cacheMu, while BuildIndex now writes `b.cache[key] = idx` under b.cacheMu.Lock() (line 137-139). Since BuildIndex no longer holds the lock for its whole body, a concurrent Prometheus scrape calling TotalDocs can race with the map write, which is a fatal Go map read/write race.
obligations: TotalDocs must not read (range over) b.cache without holding b.cacheMu (RLock or equivalent synchronization); no unsynchronized concurrent map access may remain.

The synchronization must be compatible with BuildIndex's write, which holds cacheMu.Lock() only around the single map assignment; must not reintroduce a lock held across builder()/Flush() or otherwise serialize BuildIndex, and must not deadlock.
Existing TotalDocs behavior must be preserved: return the sum of DocCount() over all cached indices, skip (continue) on any DocCount error, and keep the single int64 return signature.

The map read must see a consistent snapshot; if the iterator is released before calling DocCount on the entries, entries observed must still be the values present at iteration time (no torn/partial map state).
items.notes: Finding is accurate as written; lines 137-139 are the write and 146 the read. Valid fixes include holding cacheMu.RLock for the whole loop (simplest) or copying entries into a slice under RLock and calling DocCount outside the lock; either satisfies the obligations. Note that an RLock-held-across-DocCount approach is slightly coarser but still fine since BuildIndex's write lock is now very short. Do not 'fix' this by extending the write lock in BuildIndex over the builder; that reverts the PR intent.

items.defectStatement: In tagDeviceUI, the local cache key is written at line 87 before the call to a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice at line 93. When CreateOrUpdateDevice fails (e.g. ErrDeviceLimitReached), the function returns the error (surfaced via TagDevice at lines 144-148) but the cache entry remains, so the next request from the same device hits the cache and tagDeviceUI returns nil early, letting an over-limit device authenticate for the 29-minute cache TTL.
obligations: When CreateOrUpdateDevice fails for a device, no cache entry for that device may remain afterwards, so a subsequent request from the same device re-invokes the store instead of short-circuiting on a cache hit.

A failing CreateOrUpdateDevice (notably ErrDeviceLimitReached) must still be returned from tagDeviceUI so TagDevice propagates it and Authenticate rejects the request; the error must not be swallowed.
The success path must be preserved: on a successful store write the device's cache entry is present, and a repeat request for an already-cached device still returns nil without a store call.
The duplicate/cache hit early return, the empty-deviceID and invalid-IP early returns, and other callers of TagDevice/tagDeviceUI must keep their existing behavior.
items.notes: The finding is accurate as to the ordering at lines 87 vs 93. Valid fixes include deleting the cache key on store failure or moving localCache.SetDefault after a successful CreateOrUpdateDevice; both satisfy the obligations. The cited lines (144-148) are only the error-propagation site from the diff; the actual defect to repair is inside tagDeviceUI around lines 87-95. Note the cache key value/derivation is not shown in the window, so a fix must use the same key variable already computed in tagDeviceUI.

items.defectStatement: At line 139 the legacy write is invoked with the caller's original UpdatedObjectInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the result that unified storage already committed. Previously (see diff) the legacy call received `&updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: obj}`, where `obj` was the object returned by `d.Storage.Update`. As written, legacy storage re-evaluates `objInfo.UpdatedObject` against its own (possibly stale/divergent) old object, so the legacy patch is recomputed rather than replayed, which can yield a different result or fail even though the unified update succeeded.
obligations: The call to d.Legacy.Update must pass an update wrapper whose 'updated' object is the object returned by the preceding d.Storage.Update call (res), and whose 'upstream' is the original objInfo argument.
The d.Storage.Update call must still receive the original, unwrapped objInfo, and the returned res/async/err must still be returned unchanged from DualWriterMode3.Update.
The wrapper must preserve the upstream objInfo (e.g. for Preconditions and any other UpdatedObjectInfo methods) so legacy validation/precondition behavior is not silently dropped.

The surrounding async legacy-write structure must be preserved: legacy update still runs in the fire-and-forget goroutine with its 10s WithTimeoutCause, metrics are recorded via recordLegacyDuration, and errors there do not affect the returned result.
items.notes: The finding is confirmed by the diff: the prior code wrapped the legacy call as {upstream: objInfo, updated: obj}, so this is a regression, not an overstatement. Any expression that evaluates to the object returned by Storage.Update (e.g. `res`) as the wrapper's 'updated' is acceptable; the key is that the legacy call does NOT receive the bare objInfo and that Storage.Update still does. Out of scope but visible in the window: line 129 uses recordLegacyDuration on a storage failure, and the Delete success path passes `name` where `kind` is expected in recordStorageDuration; do not require the fix to address these.

items.defectStatement: At line 97, `parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` returns a Zod `SafeParseReturnType` wrapper (`{ success, data }`), but the whole wrapper is assigned to `key` and persisted via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. This writes the wrapper into `credential.key` instead of the parsed credential object, so the next instantiation's `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75) fails because `access_token`/`refresh_token`/`expiry_date`/`scope`/`token_type` are nested under `data` rather than top-level, permanently breaking the credential after the first token refresh.
obligations: What is written to `credential.key` must be the parsed credential object whose fields (e.g. `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `expiry_date`, `scope`, `token_type`) are at the top level, not a `{ success, data }` wrapper.
After the update, a subsequent `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (as done in `googleAuth`, line 75) must succeed with the refreshed `access_token` and `expiry_date`.

The refreshed `access_token` and `expiry_date` must still be set on the in-memory `googleCredentials` that is passed to `myGoogleAuth.setCredentials(googleCredentials)` (line 102), and the credential row must still be updated.

Parse/validation failure must not silently persist an invalid key (e.g. handle `success === false`, or use a throwing `parse`); either throwing or otherwise failing the refresh is acceptable, but writing `undefined`/a wrapper is not.
items.notes: Multiple valid fixes: `parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema).data` (with a failure check), or reverting to `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)`. A grader should accept any form that persists the top-level parsed credential while preserving the `access_token`/`expiry_date` mutation and the `prisma` update. The finding's diagnosis matches the cited diff (the prior line was `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`, which returns the parsed object, whereas `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the `safeParse` result object).

items.defectStatement: In the new backup-code branch (lines 131-157), the password verification at line 121 is guarded by `!credentials.totpCode`, and the backup-code branch is selected ahead of the TOTP branch whenever `credentials.backupCode` is set. A request supplying a non-empty dummy `totpCode` together with a valid `backupCode` therefore skips the password check entirely, never enters the TOTP verification branch, and authenticates solely on a leaked backup code plus the victim's email. The code is also irreversibly consumed (line 148-156) even though no password was verified.
obligations: A login that succeeds via `backupCode` must require the account password (or be rejected outright) — a dummy `totpCode` must not be able to suppress the password check on the backup-code path.

When both `totpCode` and `backupCode` are supplied, the request must not be authenticated by the backup code alone; either reject the combination or verify the password before accepting the backup code.

Legitimate flows must be preserved: a user with only a valid `backupCode` (no TOTP) still logs in, matching and invalidation of the consumed backup code (dash stripping, nulling the entry, re-encrypting the remainder) still happens on success, and the existing TOTP-only path (line 157+) behaves as before.
A failed authentication attempt (bad/missing password) must not consume the backup code or perform the `prisma.user.update`; the code should be removed only after all checks pass.
items.notes: The finding is accurate; the cited lines match the file. The root cause is the combination of the `!credentials.totpCode` guard on line 121 (pre-existing, intended to allow TOTP-only submissions without re-checking the password) with the backup-code branch taking precedence over the TOTP branch. Either of the two fixes named in the finding is valid, and a fix that instead verifies the password inside the backup-code branch is also acceptable. Watch that the fix does not break the SSO/third-party paths at lines 113-119, which also key off `!credentials.totpCode`, and does not regress the normal TOTP flow.

items.defectStatement: `submit` unconditionally calls `self.decoder(message.payload)` and then asserts `message.value` is a `BrokerValue`. For a bare `FilteredPayload` message value, which has no partition/offset, this assertion raises and the handler logs an error; such sentinel messages should be ignored instead. The finding is wrong that offsets are skipped: when `message.value` is a `BrokerValue`, the existing `result is None` branch or except handler already adds and completes the offset, and a bare `FilteredPayload` has no offset to track.
obligations: Bare `FilteredPayload` messages (`isinstance(message.value, FilteredPayload)`) must be ignored before decoding or asserting `BrokerValue`, without logging an error and without accessing `.partition`/`.offset`.

For `BrokerValue` messages, preserve existing offset lifecycle: a decoder `None` result adds and completes the offset; a non-None result submits a `WorkItem` with the correct partition/offset; decoder/grouping/submit exceptions still add and complete the offset.
If a `BrokerValue` carries `FilteredPayload` as its payload, its offset must still be added and completed without requiring the decoder to succeed for that case.
Do not attempt to read `partition` or `offset` from a non-`BrokerValue` value.
items.notes: The finding says `decode_payload` but the actual call is `self.decoder`. Its proposed add/complete offset for `FilteredPayload` is only possible when `message.value` is a `BrokerValue`; bare `FilteredPayload` has no offset. A valid fix may early-return for bare `FilteredPayload` and leave `BrokerValue[FilteredPayload]` to existing `None`/exception offset tracking, or explicitly handle it before decoding.

items.defectStatement: In testCacheIDPForLogin, both cleanup registrations use the literal alias "alias", which no IDP is ever created with: line 381 (inside the creation loop) should use "idp-alias-" + i and line 425 should use "idp-alias-20". As written, removing "alias" either fails immediately (NPE if the resource lookup returns null / throws NotFoundException against the REST endpoint, since no such provider exists) or silently does nothing, so the 21 IDPs created by the test (idp-alias-0..20) are not cleaned up and leak into subsequent tests.
obligations: The cleanup registered inside the creation loop (line 381) must target the alias of the provider just created in that iteration, i.e. "idp-alias-" + i (idp-alias-0 through idp-alias-19), not the literal "alias".
The cleanup registered after creating the extra provider (line 425) must target "idp-alias-20" (the alias set at line 419).

Cleanup must still be registered through getCleanup().addCleanup(...) so the created IDPs are removed at test teardown; the removal target must be obtained from the realm's identityProviders() resource by the correct alias.
No other test logic/assertions (creation flags, org associations, cache assertions, the explicit removal of idp-alias-1 at line 428) may be changed.
items.notes: The failure mode stated in the finding (NPE) is not certain: depending on whether the admin client's identityProviders().get(alias) resolves eagerly or returns a lazy resource, the wrong alias either throws NullPointerException at method-reference creation (lines 381/425) or a 404/NotFoundException when the DELETE runs during cleanup. Either way the created IDPs are not removed, which is the substantive defect. A secondary trap a fix may need to tolerate: idp-alias-1 is explicitly removed at line 428 before teardown, so a cleanup that removes every created alias could also throw for that already-removed provider (pre-existing risk, not part of the finding). Several fixes are valid (e.g. capture the alias in a local variable per iteration, or use a constant/list of created aliases).

items.defectStatement: At app/models/topic_embed.rb:13, the request-derived `url` is interpolated raw into a single-quoted `href` attribute and into the anchor's link text; a URL containing a single quote (e.g. `http://host/x'onmouseover='alert(1)`) closes the attribute and injects an event handler / arbitrary markup. The string is later cooked with `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, so the injected content is stored and rendered as raw HTML. (Correction: the only guard, line 11, is a scheme-prefix regex `/^https?\:\/\//`; there is no host validation at all, so the finding's "only its host is validated" is inaccurate — it makes the issue broader, not narrower.)
obligations: The `url` value must be HTML-escaped (attribute-safe) before being placed inside the `href='...'` attribute, so `'`, `"`, `<`, `>`, and `&` cannot terminate the attribute or introduce new attributes/tags.
The same `url` used as the anchor's visible text must also be HTML-escaped, so it cannot introduce markup.

The rendered result for an ordinary URL must be unchanged: the translated `embed.imported_from` string with a working `<a href='<url>'>` link whose href still resolves to the original URL (query strings with `&` must remain a valid href, not be mangled).

The rest of the import flow must be preserved: the line-11 scheme guard, use of the unescaped `url` for `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url)` / persistence, and the returned `post` behavior must not change.
items.notes: Any valid escaping mechanism is acceptable (ERB::Util.html_escape, CGI.escapeHTML, or constructing the anchor via Nokogiri) as long as both the attribute value and the link text are escaped and normal URLs render identically. Trap for the grader: escaping the href is correct even though it may turn `&` into `&` in the raw string — that is proper HTML and still resolves to the original URL; do not accept a fix that only strips/renames quotes or only escapes the text but leaves the href raw. A fuller fix could additionally validate the URL (host/format) at ingestion, which is a reasonable alternative but not required by the cited line. Note that `absolutize_urls` re-parses the content with Nokogiri, but it does not prevent this injection (the injected attribute survives parsing/serialization), so the fix must be on line 13 itself.

items.defectStatement: registerListener's handler gates all cleanup on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ alone, while management(session, realm) (lines 66-71) selects MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. So in a V2-only deployment (parent feature off) role/client/group removal events match no branch and permission cleanup is silently skipped; the additional claim that the both-enabled case throws UnsupportedOperationException from the V2 clients/roles/groups().setPermissionsEnabled calls is not verifiable from the cited lines and, if real, is pre-existing (the listener previously ran unconditionally).
obligations: The condition guarding the cleanup body must be true when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, including when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is not enabled, so that V2 deployments do not skip RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent cleanup merely because the V1 feature is off.

V1 behavior must be preserved: with the V1 feature enabled, RoleRemovedEvent still derives realm from role.getContainer() (client realm vs. realm itself) and calls management(session, realm).roles().setPermissionsEnabled(role, false); ClientRemovedEvent calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false); GroupRemovedEvent calls groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false).

When V2 is the active implementation, onEvent must not let an UnsupportedOperationException (or comparable failure) escape for removal events; deleting a client/role/group must still succeed. A fix may satisfy this by not invoking V2 management calls that do not support setPermissionsEnabled (e.g., skipping/keeping the V2 branch out of this listener, or using a path V2 supports).
items.notes: Only the first half of the finding is established by the cited code; the UnsupportedOperationException half lives in the V2 management classes (MgmtPermissionsV2 / ClientPermissionsV2 etc.), which are not shown, and the same call would already have been made before this change because the listener was previously unconditional — treat it as context, not as a regression introduced here. Acceptable fixes include: OR-ing ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 into the guard, explicitly using the V1 MgmtPermissions for cleanup, or conditionally skipping the V2 cleanup if V2 cannot handle it. Removing the guard entirely is also defensible (it restores the pre-change behavior where cleanup runs even with no feature enabled); graders should not require the guard to be kept. Note the guard also skips cleanup when neither feature is enabled — that is the diff's intended behavior and need not be preserved if a fix legitimately removes it.

items.defectStatement: The Silence menu action sets showSilenceDrawer=true, but the only render gate is `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`, so in the list view where `rule` is undefined and only `promRule` is supplied the silence drawer is never mounted and the action appears dead. A correct fix must open a silence flow for that Grafana-managed alerting prom rule and supply data sufficient for the silence drawer.
obligations: When `handleSilence` is invoked and `showSilenceDrawer` is true with a Grafana alerting rule supplied only as `promRule` (no `rule`), a silence drawer/flow must render; it must not be blocked solely because `rule` is undefined.
When a Grafana alerting `rulerRule` is supplied (the existing caller path), the silence drawer must still render and close as before.

The silence flow must receive enough data (rule identifier and/or rule details) to create the correct silence for the selected rule; passing `undefined` as `rulerRule` or otherwise omitting rule data is not acceptable.
Unsupported/non-Grafana-alerting rule types must remain unsilenceable, and the component should keep returning null / not throwing when no editable identifier exists.
items.notes: Finding is accurate. Trap: simply swapping the condition to `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(promRule)` may not typecheck or work because `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` expects ruler-rule data; valid fixes include extending/replacing the drawer, fetching the ruler rule on open, or otherwise deriving enough data. If `AlertRuleMenu` gates the Silence item on `rulerRule`, the symptom may be an absent menu item rather than a dead click, but the cited promRule-only render gate still prevents silence.
